articles.title: ‘Farewell he truly deserves’: Lionel Messi joins Argentina camp ahead of emotional swansong
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has joined the Argentina squad ahead of what is expected to be his final international appearance on home soil.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has joined the Argentina squad ahead of what is expected to be his final international appearance on home soil. The 39-year-old forward arrived at the team’s Ezeiza training base on Sunday and took part in his first session before the squad gathered for a traditional asado.Argentina will face Benin at the Estadio Monumental on Tuesday, with around 85,000 fans expected to attend the special occasion. The team enters the game in strong form after beating Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0.Messi will enter the farewell match with an impressive record of 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina. His international career includes winning the 2022 World Cup, two Copa America titles and the Finalissima.AFA president Claudio Tapia explained why the federation decided to organise the special event, saying: "We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina."Argentina stars set for Messi tributeSeveral of Messi’s long-time teammates will be there for his final appearance. Giovani Lo Celso, Rodrigo De Paul and Nicolas Otamendi are expected to play alongside the Argentina captain.Leandro Paredes will also attend the event from the stands despite serving a 10-match FIFA suspension following the 2026 World Cup final.However, two members of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad, Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina, will miss the occasion. Their club, AS Roma, did not allow them to travel.Messi’s next chapterArgentina will wear a special one-off kit for the occasion, featuring the Sun of May and laurel branches around Messi’s famous No. 10.After the match, Messi will return his focus to club football with Inter Miami, where he is contracted until the end of the 2028 MLS season.For Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni, the farewell also marks the beginning of a new phase as he looks to develop the next generation of players for the team’s upcoming tournament cycle.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Uruguay informa de que Martín Satriano regresa a España por "un proceso inflamatorio" en su rodilla
articles.standfirst: El atacante del Getafe estaba ejercitándose con el combinado charrúa a las órdenes de Diego Forlán
articles.summary: El atacante del Getafe estaba ejercitándose con el combinado charrúa a las órdenes de Diego Forlán
articles.body: Malas noticias para el Getafe. Martín Satriano, que estaba estas semanas a las órdenes de Diego Forlán con Uruguay, abandona la concentración charrúa después de que la federación sudamericana informase de un “proceso inflamatorio” en su rodilla. Tras comunicarse la propia federación con el conjunto azulón, ambos decidieron que lo mejor era que el delantero volviera a España para iniciar en el club su proceso de recuperación. Satriano regresaba en esta ventana de selecciones a la lista de la absoluta de su país, aventura que terminará antes de tiempo. El Getafe regresa esta semana a los entrenamientos para un regreso a la competición que trae un choque el sábado frente al FC Barcelona y el debut europeo, la próxima semana, en Rumanía frente al Universitatea Craiova. Bordalás podría perder a un Satriano al que se le seguirán realizando pruebas a su regreso.

articles.title: Vithas renueva como servicio médico oficial del Atlético de Madrid
articles.standfirst: El grupo presta cobertura sanitaria a los jugadores y cuerpo técnico de las primeras plantillas masculina y femenina, así como a sus primeros equipos filiales, desde la temporada 23/24
articles.summary: El grupo presta cobertura sanitaria a los jugadores y cuerpo técnico de las primeras plantillas masculina y femenina, así como a sus primeros equipos filiales, desde la temporada 23/24
articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid ha ampliado su acuerdo con Vithas, que continuará siendo el patrocinador oficial de servicios médicos del club durante la temporada 2026/27. La compañía sanitaria seguirá encargándose de la cobertura médica integral de los futbolistas y cuerpos técnicos de los primeros equipos masculino y femenino, así como de sus respectivos filiales. La relación entre ambas entidades se mantiene desde la campaña 2023/24, cuando Vithas asumió la atención especializada de los equipos rojiblancos a través del Centro de Medicina Deportiva de Alto Rendimiento Vithas/Invictum, ubicado en los hospitales universitarios Vithas Madrid Arturo Soria y Vithas Madrid Aravaca. Óscar Mayo, director general de Ingresos y Operaciones del Atlético de Madrid, valoró muy positivamente la renovación del acuerdo: "Estamos orgullosos de renovar nuestra colaboración con Vithas y seguir creciendo juntos después de tres temporadas. Esta renovación permitirá a nuestros equipos continuar contando con un servicio de salud de máxima calidad asistencial, respaldado por un cuadro médico de reconocido prestigio nacional e internacional". Por parte de Vithas, su CEO, el doctor Pedro Rico, agradeció la confianza depositada por el club madrileño. "Queremos agradecer la confianza que el Club Atlético de Madrid sigue depositando en Vithas y en la experiencia, talento y conocimiento que atesoran nuestros profesionales para atender las necesidades, el rendimiento y la salud de sus jugadores", señaló. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo has only one personal ambition that could make him swallow his pride and return to Portugal
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo could return to the Portugal national team as he aims for his 1000th career goal. With support from coach Jorge Jesus, the prospect of a final chapter with his country remains alive.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo may have walked away from Portugal, but there is one thing that could make even the greatest player in the country's history swallow his pride and come back.Portugal have already secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals without their captain, but the focus is now shifting back to a personal ambition Ronaldo has been chasing for years, one that could prove too important to his legacy to simply leave unfinished.Ronaldo's 1000-goal target could still lead him back to PortugalPortuguese journalist Miguel Pereira raised the possibility of a Ronaldo return before Portugal's latest meeting with Norway, when the fallout from his departure was still unfolding and the two sides had yet to play their second match against one another.Speaking to talkSPORT, Pereira argued that Ronaldo had a specific reason for wanting the final stretch of his extraordinary scoring record to involve Portugal, rather than simply completing the milestone during his club career with Al Nassr.“The thing is that 21 goals that he needs to score [to reach his 1000th]. He really wanted to score the last one with Portugal the same way that Pelé mounted a show when he scored his 1000th goal, and I think he was aiming to score that goal at the end of the season in a match with Portugal,” Pereira said.Pereira believed Ronaldo had expected to score around 15 to 20 goals for Al Nassr during the season before creating an occasion around the landmark strike, allowing him to celebrate what would be one of the defining moments of his career in front of the Portuguese supporters.“He was expecting to score the 15-20 goals during the season easily with Al Nassr, but he really wanted to throw up a party that celebrates himself, his ego, his history with the national side,” Pereira added.That possibility looked considerably harder to imagine when Ronaldo left the Portugal camp, although Pereira still believed the relationship could eventually be repaired.Jorge Jesus has now reopened the door for RonaldoPortugal went on to beat Norway 2–1 on Sunday, October 4, at the Estádio do Dragão, giving Jorge Jesus four wins from four in Group A4 and making Portugal the first team to officially secure a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.They achieved that without Ronaldo, who had left the squad after Jesus decided against using him against Norway despite sending him to warm up for around 30 minutes.Jesus has now offered the clearest indication yet that the departure does not have to become permanent, telling reporters after the Norway victory that Ronaldo remains eligible for the next squad selection provided he continues playing and chooses to return.“For me, Cristiano will be eligible for selection the next time the squad is announced, provided he is playing. If he wants to, he will return to the national team,” Jesus said.The Portugal coach also made clear that the final decision rests with Ronaldo, saying: “If he wants to, he'll return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who's going to decide.”That statement has changed the tone around a possible comeback, particularly because Ronaldo himself has not announced a decision either way since promising that he would explain the reasons for his departure “in due time”.Ronaldo's camp and Portugal still have a way backPereira had argued before the Norway match, that the bridges between Ronaldo's camp and the Portuguese setup could still be rebuilt.“But right now I really do think there are bridges being built between Cristiano’s camp, Jesus’ camp, the Portuguese federation is very much interested in having Cristiano because of all the publicity it gets, and I do think that Cristiano will be back for a last dance with the Portuguese side later next year,” Pereira said.Portugal now have their quarter-final place secured, Jesus has publicly left the decision with Ronaldo, and the forward still has a major personal milestone within reach. articles.title: Hugo Galdeano, un talento gigante para el Barça
articles.standfirst: El menudo atacante de La Masía brilla por su nivel de juego y su garra… siendo el más chiquito de toda la categoría
articles.summary: El menudo atacante de La Masía brilla por su nivel de juego y su garra… siendo el más chiquito de toda la categoría
articles.body: Con 12 años hay niños que han pegado el ‘estirón’ y otros que lo dejan para un poco más adelante. El caso de Hugo Galdeano, hijo de exfutbolista, es de los que se está cocinando a fuego lento. El más menudo del equipo, pero también del torneo, es el niño con más talento, con bastante diferencia, de los que pisó los campos de la ESPN en Orlando. El Barça tiene en el hijo de Apoño un diamante que reluce con fuerza. El chico tiene regate, disparo, desparpajo a raudales y sobre todo, una visión de juego que es imposible entrenar. Le sale natural. Un pase filtrado, un ligero toque para poner a un compañero en ventaja, un centro medido, una pisada con la cabeza mirando al frente. En definitiva un estilo de juego muy La Masía y bastante reconocible en los mejores jugadores del mundo. “Mi ídolo es Pedri, he aprendido mucho de él y ya le he conocido”, asegura cuando se le pregunta por sus referente. No ha elegido mal jugador al que seguir de cerca. Al margen de la calidad Hugo tiene características, lo necesita. Con su físico, o planta cara y va a todas o a esta edad, con chicos por encima del 1.75 cm tiene poco que hacer. En este último torneo de Orlando se hizo viral un enganchón con un jugador del Betis un par de palmos más grande que él. Acabó con expulsión de un minuto al rincón de pensar. En el aspecto de la popularidad, el chico tampoco se queda corto. Su cuenta de Instagram, obviamente controlada y gestionada por su familia, cuenta con 180.000 seguidores y en ellas se puede comprobar que una multinacional como Nike ya le ha echado el lazo pensando en el futuro que le puede esperar.

articles.title: Player welfare, injury worries & boredom - has extended international break worked?
articles.summary: The extended international break was brought in with player welfare in mind, but has it been a success?
articles.body:
The first international break of the 2026-27 season is almost over - and it has been a longer one than fans are used to.

For the first time, the Premier League and Championship paused for three weeks rather than the usual two with players returning to domestic action from Friday.

The idea was brought in by Fifa with player welfare in mind, but, with a growing list of injuries, has it really been a success?

Who benefits from an extended international schedule? And do people really want a three-week break from domestic action when the season has only just got going?

In recent years, Fifa has used five primary international breaks during the season, all consisting of two-week gaps in March, June, September, October and November.

The switch to a three-week gap across late September and early October, alongside reducing the number of breaks down to four, was made for a number of reasons .

One was that the scheduling of the 2026 World Cup final on 19 July was the latest date for a summer World Cup since 1966.

Player welfare also featured in the discussions, this including travel considerations.

The reduction in the number of breaks will reduce the number of journeys some players face in having to travel from one continent to another for their international fixtures . One such example is African and South American players who play their domestic football in Europe and have to travel cross-continent to fulfil international fixtures.

But with the domestic season just starting to get interesting, fans tend to bemoan the interruption - no matter the length - and long for the return of club football.

The extended international break might have been brought in with player welfare in mind, but the reality is that a number of players will return to their clubs with injuries.

It is hard to quantify whether more injuries have been picked up during the past fortnight than during other international breaks and it must be factored in that this is a lengthier break with more fixtures. A full and fair comparison might have to wait until the end of the season, after all the international breaks.

However, there have been numerous injuries to players since players joined up with international team-mates.

On Monday, it was announced that Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott had withdrawn from the England squad with a thigh injury and the Cherries are unhappy with the way they believe England handled the injury.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland asked to be substituted on 67 minutes, subsequently limping off in Norway's match against Portugal on Sunday before leaving camp on Monday while club team-mate Nico O'Reilly returned to City for further assessment.

Following the injury to Haaland, the Norwegian players' union (NISO) expressed concern over the increased demands.

"Over time, we have seen a worrying trend where the burden on top players has become far too high," NISO chief Kristoffer Vatshaug said.

"We want clearer guidelines for workload and recovery. It is about the time between matches, consecutive rest periods, travel strain and how much time players get to recover after a long season."

Liverpool duo Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak have both picked up injuries with Gakpo withdrawing from the Netherlands squad with an ankle injury and Isak pulling out of Sweden duty with a minor thigh injury.

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus revealed Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes had been playing through pain while Sunderland's Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey both sustained hamstring problems.

Club managers will have their fingers crossed that no more names are added to that list with three days of fixtures still to be played.

England's Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice all pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's squad before the start of the break.

Away from the Premier League, there have also been injuries to some of the biggest stars in the game with Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe sustaining an injury while on duty with France and Barcelona's Raphinha also returned from Brazil with a thigh injury.

'More challenging' but 'positives to take' - Tuchel

England boss Thomas Tuchel has previously been critical of the three-week break, saying it is "more challenging" than previous years, citing travel and having only two days of rest between games as problems.

In a news conference on Monday before England take on the Czech Republic on Tuesday he said: "I can assure everyone that player welfare is priority number one.

"But new training styles and training times, different positions to play maybe, increase the chance of injury."

On whether the extended break has had an impact on injuries, he said "we need to get the numbers right" before deciding.

"Is it really more or is it the same amount [of games] as in two shorter little windows? I don't have the answer to that," he said.

"The two-week window is not guilty for everything. If it is a thing, we will adapt and make the most of it as always.

"I didn't like the start of it after a long tournament to have a long window. There are also positives to it like we saw against Croatia after having three matches together.

"The team is together for longer, more training sessions, more meetings, more of the same language. You see improvements and automatisms clicking in. We made it a very good camp."

Shay, Swindon: I don't think any Premier League or Championship fan backs this idea. It's just boring without your club in action for so long.

James McCreadie: Fans are getting sick and tired of losing players to what is a glorified friendly. Teams in Europe and Carabao Cup have nine games in 28 days or so before the next international break. Hope clubs pull players out, citing that player welfare comes first.

Matt, York: The amount of injuries during this break, most of them muscular, including the usually extremely robust Erling Haaland surely highlights it has been a mistake of an experiment. Whoever thought it a good idea after a long World Cup summer needs to be in for a performance review.

Kelvin Thomas: Too many players are being withdrawn due to injuries. But I am sure they will make a miraculous recovery when back at there clubs. Even with them gone England will win (bring it on).

James: Revealing that players came to camp with minor issues highlights the pointed comments about Cole Palmer (and I'm sure others) who seem to value their club more than country. Last chance saloon for a few of them come next internationals.

The international break signals an opportunity for fans to swap their usual Premier League or Championship ticket for a trip to a local lower league club or Women's Super League match.

Women's teams associated with a Premier League club often take the opportunity to play their home matches at the larger men's stadium to allow more fans to attend.

Without tiers one and two of the football pyramid in action, it also means room on the television schedule for lower-league matches - a financial boost for those clubs.

While it is difficult to compare week by week attendances because of the number of variables, the international break does offer some fans the chance to watch other teams in action.

Across the 11 games played in League One and League Two on Saturday – nine postponed because of international call-ups – only three had attendances less than their home average for the season.

In the WSL, five of the seven games played over the weekend had a higher attendance than the home club's season average.

articles.title: Pau Cubarsí encabeza la lista final de 25 candidatos al 'Golden Boy' 2026
articles.standfirst: 'Tuttosport' publicó hoy la lista en un evento en Venecia con la presencia de MARCA
articles.summary: 'Tuttosport' publicó hoy la lista en un evento en Venecia con la presencia de MARCA
articles.body: Ya sabemos la lista final de 25 candidatos que lucharán por ser el 'Golden Boy by Transfermarkt' 2026, el prestigioso galardón individual que distingue al mejor jugador Sub 21 de un club europeo en el período que va de diciembre 2025 a diciembre 2026. El diario italiano 'Tuttosport', organizador del certamen, lanzó hoy la lista oficial en un evento en el majestuoso Palacio de la Banca Ifis en Venecia en el que participó MARCA como uno de los votantes a nivel español. El ganador final será desvelado a principios de diciembre en la habitual gala de Turín. Entre los 25 candidatos (20+5 'wild cards' designados por el organizador) este año aparece como gran favorito el central del Barça Pau Cubarsí. El jugador del Barça ganó la Liga con el club azulgrana e hizo un Mundial, y una final, extraordinarios. Es el gran favorito a ser el 'chico de oro', ya que su compañero Lamine Yamal no lo puede ganar de nuevo, pues fue el Golden Boy en 2024. El galardón busca este año al mejor Sub 21 nacido a partir del 1 de enero del 2006 con la particularidad de que este premio, desde su nacimiento, nunca puede tener ganador repetido, por lo que Lamine Yamal está excluido como posible vencedor. Cubarsí aparece en los primeros cinco puestos de los candidatos (creados por el algoritmo de 'Transfermarkt') junto a otros talentos como Luka Vuskovic (Brighton); Ayyoub Bouaddi (Man. City); el madridista Yan Diomande; o el francés Marren Zaire-Emery (PSG). Ellos son los favoritos pero hay otros candidatos, hasta llegar al puesto número 20. Entre ellos, están el madridista Endrick o el barcelonista Marc Bernal. Los cinco 'wild cards', que no estaban entre los 20 candidatos creados por los algoritmos de Transfermarkt, son Kostoulas, (Brighton); Rodrigo Mora (Roma); Joane Gadou (Dortmund); Franco Mastantuono (Fiorentina); y el español Xavi Espart (Barça). Todos podrán ser votados ahora por el Jurado internacional. A partir de hoy, ese jurado internacional de 50 periodistas europeos de 27 países diferentes, entre los que está MARCA como medio, será el encargado de elegir el ganador final. Cada periodista de esos 50 vota por cinco nombres, de más a menos (1, el favorito, 2, 3, 4 y 5). Así sale el ganador. Una de las personalidades presentes fue la leyenda uruguaya Paolo Montero, exjugador de la Juventus, entre otros, que dijo sobre Cubarsí: "Hacer lo que ha hecho Pau, con ese nivel de presión, es absolutamente propio de un jugador de extraordinario valor. La cantera de España lleva produciendo ese tipo de jugadores hace muchos años y es para valorarlo". El primer Golden Boy de todos, allá por 2003, fue Raphael Van der Vaart y el último fue el francés del PSG Désiré Doué (2025). El ganador de esta edición 2026 ya está en votación y se conocerá a principios de diciembre... con el claro favoritismo de Pau Cubarsí (Barça).

articles.title: Ex-Manchester leader defends deals with Man City owners
articles.summary: Veteran former council leader Sir Richard Leese says the relationship has been beneficial to the city.
articles.body:
The former leader of Manchester City Council has defended the council's relationship with the owners of Manchester City amid questions over land deals.

Sir Richard Leese, who was head of the council for 25 years until 2021 and is also honorary president of the club, said a decade-old deal with Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) was "good for the city".

The partnership between the authority and the company owned by Sheik Mansour bin zayed Al Nahyan has come under renewed scrutiny since City was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations with "sham" commercial contracts .

The club has denied any wrongdoing is appealing against the charges.

The council entered into a partnership with ADUG in 2014 when they formed a joint venture called Manchester Life.

It planned to invest more than £1bn over the next decade and develop thousands of homes in the Ancoats and New Islington areas, on the edge of the city centre close to the club's Etihad stadium.

But in 2022, a report by the University of Sheffield, called Manchester Offshored, raised questions about the wider public value of the schemes, and a lack of transparency around their finances.

It highlighted the absence of any affordable housing in the projects, and that the joint venture companies were ultimately owned by ADUG through firms registered offshore.

A deal struck in 2015 saw ADUG effectively given the first pick of land in Ancoats and New Islington. The University of Sheffield report argued that land was leased to ADUG at "below comparable rates".

Sir Richard said the 2015 deal was "brokered by the UK government with the UAE government".

"It was a time when development in Manchester had stopped," he said.

"We were still suffering from the 2008 crash, from the recession that followed that.

"There was criticism at the time though - and there still is now - that the land was given away too cheaply by the city council.

"The point is, the investment from Abu Dhabi is what created the value.

"That deal allowed development to be kick-started - particularly in the Ancoats area.

"All of this was documented and went through reports that went through the council's due processes.

"I think it has been demonstrated that the deal was a good deal and a good deal for Manchester."

Abu Dhabi's investment in Manchester City started in 2008, when City Football Group – majority-owned by ADUG - bought the club in a £200m deal.

With significant investment from its new owners, the club went on to win its first trophy in 36 years with an FA Cup win in 2011 and a dramatic Premier League title followed the next year.

The club went on to win the league seven more times between 2013 and 2024.

But the Premier League began investigating the club's financial dealings in 2018, and City was charged in 2023.

Last week, it was announced the club had been found guilty of 115 charges, including some around a so-called disguised funding scheme, which was said to have seen the club's owners topping up sponsorship and commercial deals with their own funding running to more than £800m.

When asked last week about potential fallout from the City charges, Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who was metropolitan mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026, said he would be "really concerned" if the owners were to pull out of the club.

He added: "They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

Since then, it has been reported that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) may halt UK-wide investment schemes worth billions of pounds as a result of the Premier League ruling.

Sir Richard said he hoped that Manchester did not lose UEA investment, adding: "I think certainly Abu Dhabi will be thinking that they have been very badly treated given the contribution that they have made - not just to Manchester but to English football as well."

He added: "I would be concerned if they did stop investing. I don't think they'd give us up."

Sir Richard told BBC Radio 4's Today programme earlier that "the investment in Manchester from Abu Dhabi has been very significant".

Stressing he was not speaking on behalf of the club, he pointed to the investment in City, its training complex and the City Football Group headquarters.

He added: "I think for the city, one thing about working with Abu Dhabi is everything that they promised they have delivered.

"So they have real credibility in the city. That's something we'd want to maintain.

"I don't think any other football club has got anywhere near the sort of contribution that they have made to their local community.

"What has been created in Manchester City is a phenomenon really and that has to be maintained in some way whatever the final outcome of the allegations against them."

Manchester City Council also defended the benefits of the partnership with Manchester Life as a "platform for future development".

"The claim that working in partnership with Manchester City's owners has not been a good deal for the council or the city has been debunked repeatedly," the authority said.

"Claims that some land was sold too cheaply to Manchester Life ignore the fact that there was zero market interest at the time of the sale, that the land is worth more now precisely because of Manchester Life's investment and the significant financial return the council is receiving through profit-sharing arrangements.

"Manchester Life was always envisaged as a platform for further investment. Its success should be measured in what it has delivered directly and what it has unlocked.

"The partnership was set up to deliver significant housing development, create an investor confidence and a platform for other developers to come into the market and invest in Manchester - which it has achieved."

articles.title: Quique Sánchez Flores, operado de una lesión de rodilla
articles.standfirst: El conjunto babazorro ha adelantado la noticia en las fuentes personales del club
articles.summary: El conjunto babazorro ha adelantado la noticia en las fuentes personales del club
articles.body: Sorpresa en Mendizorroza por una nueva lesión. La cuestión es que no ha sido de ningún jugador, sino de su técnico, Quique Sánchez Flores. Al parecer el entrenador tenía unas molestias en la rodilla que debían ser reparadas y ya ha sido intervenido quirúrgicamente. El entrenador de 61 años atraviesa un momento irregular en el banquillo babazorro tras dos derrotas y un empate en los últimos tres encuentros. El próximo será este sabado en Mendizorroza ante el Atlético de Madrid. Un partido en el que parece que sí podrá estar para dirigirlo. El conjunto babazorro ha informado de la operación con el siguiente comunicado: El entrenador del Deportivo Alavés, Quique Sánchez Flores, ha sido intervenido quirúrgicamente de una lesión en su rodilla y evoluciona favorablemente tras la operación. La intervención, llevada a cabo por los doctores Manuel Leyes y César Flores, se ha desarrollado con normalidad y el técnico se encuentra bien. El entrenador albiazul continuará desarrollando su actividad habitual al frente del primer equipo durante su recuperación.

articles.title: Las 21 'averías' del Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: La lesión de Asencio es el último gran golpe que recibe el equipo en forma de lesión
articles.summary: La lesión de Asencio es el último gran golpe que recibe el equipo en forma de lesión
articles.body: La importante lesión de Asencio es el último gran golpe que recibe el Madrid en forma de lesión. Están siendo temporadas especialmente desafortunadas en la enfermería madridista y la reciente operación del defensa es una prueba más de ello. Las bajas de larga duración se han convertido en uno de los grandes enemigos del conjunto blanco en los últimos tiempos. El Madrid lleva unos años en los que las lesiones de gravedad están a la orden del día. Y la actual campaña ya ha puesto el contador en marcha con la operación de Asencio, que estará aproximadamente cuatro meses fuera de combate. Con Asencio son ya 21 'averías' importantes las que ha sufrido el Real Madrid en las cuatro últimas temporadas. O lo que es lo mismo, la plantilla madridista ha sufrido 21 lesiones de dos meses o más de baja. Un listón temporal que ya tiene consecuencias más allá del problema físico en cuestión: una larga inactividad que complica el regreso a la competición, aleja al jugador de su mejor estado físico, lo descuelga del resto de sus compañeros y aumenta el riesgo de nuevas lesiones. Asencio ya ha estrenado el casillero de 'averías' en el Madrid, que la pasada temporada se elevó hasta las nueve lesiones de gravedad, que afectaron a ocho jugadores. Tres de ellos aún no han vuelta a estar disponibles desde que se lesionaron la pasada campaña: Militao, Mendy y Rodrygo. Además, Rüdiger estuvo 79 días de baja, Trent 67 y Carvajal 74. Bellingham, operado del hombro al final de la 24-25, y Endrick, que recayó en el Mundial de Clubes de la lesión en el tendón conjunto de los isquiotibiales de la pierna derecha arrancaron la temporada en la enfermería, pagaron caros ambos contratiempos físicos. El inglés, golpeado por otra lesión muscular más adelante, no encontró la pasada temporada su mejor versión hasta el reciente Mundial, donde brilló con Inglaterra. Endrick se descolgó tras quedarse sin pretemporada y acabó cedido al Lyon en el mercado de enero. Carvajal no renovó, Trent tuvo una temporada de debut como madridista muy gris y sólo Rüdiger consiguió remontar y ganarse la renovación por un año más. En la 24-25 la lesiones de gravedad también hicieron acto de presencia para 'dinamitar' al Madrid. El primer golpe duro fue la gravísima lesión de rodilla de Carvajal, de la que precisamente hoy se cumplen dos años. Ancelotti perdía a uno de sus grandes líderes dentro y fuera del campo a principios de octubre. Por si fuera poco, un mes después perdía otra vez a Militao, que se rompía otra vez el ligamento cruzado, esta vez de la pierna derecha. Luego, casi sin tregua, llegarían las graves lesiones de Camavinga (77 días de baja), Alaba (65), Mendy (179) y Rüdiger (60). El muro del Madrid se hacía añicos golpeado por los contratiempos físicos. En la 23-24 fueron otras cinco lesiones de gravedad. En julio ya cayeron Ceballos y Güler, que vieron condicionado su comienzo de temporada con dos lesiones de más de dos meses de baja. Especialmente crítico fue el mes de agosto, en el que Courtois y Militao, en un margen de tres días, se rompieron el ligamento cruzado. En diciembre, Alaba firmaría el desgraciado triplete de cruzados en el Real Madrid.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reaparece tras la tormenta
articles.standfirst: El portugués ha vuelto a los entrenamientos de Al-Nassr
articles.summary: El portugués ha vuelto a los entrenamientos de Al-Nassr
articles.body: Como se suele decir, después de la tormenta llega la calma. Y en el caso de Cristiano Ronaldo, se trata de su vuelta a Arabia Saudí para regresar a los entrenamientos con Al-Nassr. Tras todo el caos generado alrededor de su figura, después de que el luso abandonase la concentración de Portugal en plena Nations League, Cristiano ya vuelve a ponerse en marcha para alcanzar su máximo objetivo: llegar a los 1.000 goles. Ahora mismo, el portugués lleva 979, a tan solo 21 goles de alcanzar las cuatro cifras. Ha sumado tres a la lista en el arranque de temporada, y no parece que vaya a parar hasta alcanzar los 1.000. La pasada campaña llegó a los 30 tantos, por lo que si logra igualar el ritmo, llegará esta misma temporada. Todo apunta a que, de conseguirlo, será vistiendo la camiseta del Al-Nassr, con el que se ha reincorporado hoy, al igual que sus compañeros que no han acudido al parón con sus respectivas selecciones, como Mané, Coman, Íñigo Martínez, Samú Costa o Simakan. El viernes 9 de octubre se dará su regreso al verde, enfrentando a Al Diriyah para intentar revalidar el título de liga. El propio Cristiano compartió tras su primer entrenamiento con sus compañeros unas imágenes en las que se le ve sonriendo, bromeando con el resto de la plantilla de Al-Nassr, un cambio radical respecto a su amargo adiós a Portugal.

articles.title: El Málaga suma a su red de canteras un caladero histórico de futbolistas
articles.standfirst: Acuerdo con El Palo FC para el acuerdo marco provincial
articles.summary: Acuerdo con El Palo FC para el acuerdo marco provincial
articles.body: El Málaga CF sigue ampliando su red de clubes convenidos. Lo hace con discreción, pero dando pasos importantes para reforzar el proyecto de cantera que puso en marcha Loren Juarros desde su llegada a La Rosaleda. Según puede avanzar Radio MARCA Málaga, el próximo nombre importante que se incorporará al Acuerdo Marco será El Palo FC. El conjunto de San Ignacio permanecía hasta ahora al margen, junto a otros clubes que todavía no habían cerrado su incorporación al proyecto. Un movimiento que ya ha recibido el visto bueno y que está pendiente únicamente de la firma. Carlos Dávila, gerente de La Academia, confirmó esta misma semana en los micrófonos de Radio MARCA Málaga que el acuerdo está prácticamente cerrado. “Con El Palo y el Mijas Las Lagunas nos han dado el ‘okey’ esta semana y simplemente estamos pendientes de firmar el acuerdo estos próximos días”, explicó Dávila en directo. La incorporación de El Palo supone un paso relevante para el Málaga por el peso que el fútbol base paleño ha tenido históricamente como fuente de talento para el fútbol malagueño. A su lado también se incorpora el Mijas Las Lagunas, que atraviesa además un momento histórico después de debutar esta temporada en el Grupo IV de Segunda RFEF. El conjunto mijeño logró recientemente su primera victoria en la categoría tras golear por 6-2 al Tamaraceite. Dos nuevas incorporaciones que refuerzan una estructura de cantera que esta misma semana volvió a mostrar músculo con la presentación oficial de los equipos de La Academia. El acuerdo entre el Málaga y El Palo FC conecta a dos clubes separados por apenas unos kilómetros, pero también vuelve a poner en valor una de las grandes canteras futbolísticas de Málaga. La barriada ha sido cuna o lugar de formación de numerosos jugadores que llegaron al fútbol profesional, con al menos 13 futbolistas que alcanzaron Primera o Segunda División. Entre ellos aparecen nombres históricos como Juan Galacho, Manolito Rodríguez, los hermanos Nacho y Juan Carlos Pérez Frías, Basti, Francis Bravo, Carlos Aranda, Manolo Gaspar, Recio, Francisco Portillo, Alberto Escassi y Rafa de Vicente. Una nómina de varias generaciones que explica la profunda tradición futbolística de El Palo y su capacidad para seguir produciendo jugadores de alto nivel.

articles.title: OFFSIDE | Why Sir Alex Ferguson vs Pep Guardiola is no longer a debate
articles.summary: Sir Alex Ferguson built dynasties from Aberdeen to Old Trafford, while Pep Guardiola has spent his career managing football’s richest and most powerful institutions. With Manchester City’s financial breaches and Barcelona’s Negreira affair now part of the historical record, the old debate over who was the greater manager looks increasingly lopsided.
articles.body: Hello and welcome to another edition of Offside.One of the side effects of democracy is that people have too many asinine opinions that they feel the need to air, including questioning gospel truths by wondering if Babar Azam can be compared to Sachin Tendulkar or if Hyderabadi biryani is a better gustatory offering than Kolkata biryani. To quote the Pakistani viral guy: Khuda ka khauf karo. Yet, some even have the temerity to make the blasphemous suggestion that Pep Guardiola is a better manager than Sir Alex Ferguson. They somehow believe that the man who has only managed clubs with transfer budgets that could be the GDP of a nation is comparable with Ferguson’s footballing legacy.Can you imagine Guardiola taking a club like Aberdeen, breaking up the Old Firm hegemony and then going to the Cup Winners’ Cup to beat Real Madrid with a team from Aberdeen? Or taking a relegation-threatened team known more for being a social club than a football club and converting it into perennial winners with a force of personality that held a massive club together despite a huge debt, only for the club to immediately collapse when he left?Now that doesn’t mean Guardiola is a bad football coach. He is a genius who understood the geometry of football better than anyone else, but he did it with clubs like Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City that spent a league’s budget on fullbacks.Perhaps it’s the timing that makes the terms of the debate even more hollow.As Guardiola’s City legacy is thrown under a shadow by the independent commission’s findings, Ferguson’s new book is upon us: Games of My Life.The book is built around 21 matches from a footballing career that spanned 69 years as a player and manager, encompassing more than 2,800 official fixtures, and even then the 1999 Champions League final doesn’t make the cut.As Ferguson put it, in the line that truly explains the difference between a manager and a coach, the games that stayed with him were often about the people rather than the games.It will be a fascinating follow-up to Ferguson’s older books and will perhaps explain how an apprentice toolmaker from Govan, whose certificate listed his skills as “milling, shaping, slotting, turning and all forms of grinding”, managed to use those skills to create dynasty after dynasty of footballing legends.Ferguson’s real genius was never drawing arrows on a whiteboard. Before he became the red-nosed benevolent dictator at United, he was a trade-union shop steward who went on strike, taking his apprentices with him, because he believed it was his duty towards the group.Years later, it was the same system, except the apprentices were multimillionaire footballers and the industrial action was knocking Liverpool off their f***** perch.Ferguson often used Lunch atop a Skyscraper – the famous image of construction workers calmly eating hundreds of feet above Manhattan – to tell young footballers that if those men weren’t concerned about falling, then perhaps they shouldn’t be concerned about going in for a tackle.Hear any player speak about him and you get the feeling that they would have powered through brick walls and mountains for Ferguson. Perhaps Guardiola too evokes that sort of loyalty.There used to be a saying in English football about Lionel Messi: but can he do it on a cold, rainy night in Stoke? Could his mentor Pep Guardiola ever do it on a cold night in Aberdeen? It’s a big What If for a man who has only managed Barcelona, with some of the world’s most gifted footballers and the greatest to ever play the game; Bayern Munich, where even the kitman can win the league; and Manchester City, whose books were so cooked, according to the Premier League commission’s findings, that it now looks like a Breaking Bad sequel.Strip away the footballers that City could attract for Guardiola and wonder if those trophies would still be there. On the other hand, Ferguson won league titles with Tom Cleverley, Darron Gibson and Anderson.Much the same team with which Ferguson won the league finished seventh a year later under David Moyes. In the Fergie era, coming second was considered an abject failure. Post-Fergie, it was a high point.But Guardiola’s performance at City, where he also won the Treble, opened the gate for a debate and perhaps, looking at a piece of paper, there’s an argument to be made. In his ten years at City, he won the league six times and a total of 17 major trophies, excluding Community Shields. In 27 years, Ferguson won only 28 major trophies, excluding Charity Shields.But Guardiola took over a team that had already won two Premier League titles in the previous five seasons, had reached the Champions League semi-finals the season before he arrived, and contained Sergio Agüero, Kevin De Bruyne, David Silva, Fernandinho, Vincent Kompany and Raheem Sterling.Not exactly Aberdeen.And then consider the money.Depending on how transfer fees and add-ons are calculated, during Guardiola’s decade City spent roughly £2 billion. Fergie broke British transfer records too, but during Ferguson’s final eight seasons under the Glazers, United spent £343 million gross and only around £153 million net on players, while almost £496 million left the club in interest payments. Ferguson still won five Premier League titles in those eight seasons.And then we come to FFP, which leaves the true asterisk hanging over Guardiola’s City legacy.We now know that the Premier League’s independent commission found that City had inflated revenues and concealed costs during the period from 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the financial distortion exceeding £900 million. That period included the season in which Guardiola’s City finished with 100 points.So, on one hand, you have a manager working under severe financial constraints brought on by the Glazer buyout of Manchester United. Ferguson was never particularly candid about his time under the Glazers, refusing calls from hardcore fans to step down and insisting that he needed to be there for the club.Contrast that with Guardiola, who left before the verdict came out.After it did, he posted: “I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever.”Except he wasn’t. He had already left.A similar shadow hangs over Guardiola’s time at Barcelona because of the Negreira affair, in which Barcelona paid more than €7.3 million over 17 years to companies linked to José María Enríquez Negreira, then vice-president of Spain’s refereeing committee. Barcelona says the money was for technical reports on referees, and no evidence has established that referees were paid to fix matches. Unfortunately for Pep, his entire Barcelona reign fell within the payment period.And then history decides to provide a joke that would have been rejected by a scriptwriter for being too obvious.Many years ago, Guardiola’s mentor Johan Cruyff told Ferguson: “You’ll never win the European Cup.”Ferguson asked: “Why?”Cruyff replied: “You don’t cheat and you don’t buy referees.”Guardiola is not accused of participating in either the Negreira affair or City’s financial breaches. But both controversies sit squarely inside his two most successful managerial eras, which means they will inevitably cast a long shadow over how those achievements are remembered.Earlier, one could at least fathom why people were willing to debate Guardiola versus Ferguson.Now, with the City findings and the Negreira affair added to the historical record, the argument becomes much harder to make. There was never a meaningful debate.The UK-UAE KerfuffleSince David Cameron called for the ill-fated Brexit Referendum, the UK has had seven Prime Ministers, the latest being the “King of the North”, Andy Burnham, who just happens to be a little too pally with the Man City owners, and might just find his head on the chopping block soon.Before he became PM, he spent nine years as mayor of Greater Manchester, during which time he repeatedly praised the Abu Dhabi ownership for investing in the club and in east Manchester. After the guilty verdict, he even put his neck out and said he would be “really concerned” if City lost their owners.The Financial Times revealed that City chairman Khaldoon al-Mubarak, one of Abu Dhabi’s most powerful officials and the man who also runs the £290 billion Mubadala investment empire, has held diplomatic immunity in Britain since 2020, shielding him from criminal prosecution and most civil proceedings in the UK.The Daily Mail reported that Abu Dhabi warned the British government as far back as 2023 that an adverse outcome in City’s case could damage UK-UAE relations. The Mail also found that the Manchester Life partnership had first refusal on large development sites, and Manchester City Council received no rental income till 2023-24 even as Mansour-linked companies earned more than £39 million over five years.Given the UK’s modern love for swapping Prime Ministers, it’s not unlikely that Burnham’s linkages to the UAE become the albatross around his premiership’s neck.India vs Brazil: What the 4-0 actually showedThat India would lose to Brazil was a given, but there was more to see than the 4-0 scoreline would suggest. For a while, India actually inconvenienced Brazil before the natural course of things took over, and perhaps we should take heart from that. Khalid Jamil’s side stayed organised, defended with discipline and showed that they could at least make one of the world’s best teams work for their goals.The gulf in quality eventually told, as it was always going to. But for once, a heavy defeat did not feel entirely pointless.“No time for idiots”Jürgen Klopp has always kept it simple, on and off the pitch. Asked about the latest debate over whether his Germany team was “German enough” or “white enough”, Klopp dismissed it as “complete nonsense”, adding that he had little time in everyday life for idiocy and even less on social media.The depressing part is that German football has been here before.When Germany crashed out of the 2018 World Cup, Mesut Özil, born in Gelsenkirchen to Turkish parents and a World Cup winner four years earlier, believed he had suddenly become the convenient face of failure. Announcing his international retirement, he delivered perhaps the definitive line on conditional European nationalism: “I am German when we win, but I am an immigrant when we lose.”The Artist is long gone but it would appear that for German football, the race albatross hangs around its neck, rearing its head whenever a coloured man can be blamed.Ronaldo vs MessiSpeaking of pointless debates, it has become rather tiresome to see Cristiano Ronaldo’s descent into a petulant non-entity. While Messi is turning up for one last dance with Argentina, Ronaldo has gone home from the Portugal camp after throwing a fit. On Football Twitter – and other places where fans discuss the Beautiful Game – Ronaldo has often been labelled “Homelander”, the antagonist of The Boys, a superhero figure with severe narcissistic personality disorder.And the late-stage careers of Messi and Ronaldo are starting to resemble the final fight between Billy Butcher and Homelander after the latter loses his powers. While Messi still seems to have some stardust left, as we saw with Argentina during the World Cup, Ronaldo’s race seems run. It’s a tragic sight for all of us who watched him grow up, going from a winger of touch and tease to one of the best footballers in the world. One never knows the right time to retire. Take Novak Djokovic, who showed Alexander Zverev how it’s done recently, but a similar redemption looks quite unlikely for Ronaldo.Perhaps that is the only opponent neither Messi nor Ronaldo could ever beat: Father Time comes for us all. articles.title: Sorloth y Lookman vuelven al grupo
articles.standfirst: El noruego se incorpora tras dos meses de lesión, mientras que el nigeriano adelanta su regreso tras ser liberado por Nigeria
articles.summary: El noruego se incorpora tras dos meses de lesión, mientras que el nigeriano adelanta su regreso tras ser liberado por Nigeria
articles.body: La primera sesión de entrenamiento de la última semana del parón ha traído buenas noticias al Atlético en forma de novedades, pues Simeone ya cuenta en su aún reducido grupo con dos efectivos mas: Sorloth y Lookman. El noruego, tras dos meses en la enfermería, por fin ve la luz para poner fin a un calvario que comenzaría en su primera semana de trabajo con una contractura y que, tras una recaída y varios retrocesos en su recuperación, ha acabado derivando en una inactividad que aún no le ha permitido estrenarse en este curso. Ahora, por fin, ya encara su regreso definitivo, postulándose (aunque su incorporación será progresiva, tal y como quedó patente en una sesión que empezó con sus compañeros y prosiguió en el gimnasio) para viajar el viernes a Vitoria si en las próximos ensayos evoluciona según lo esperado. La otra gran novedad del ensayo sería la presencia de Lookman a pesar de que a Nigeria aún le queda un compromiso frente a Rusia. En este sentido, al tratarse de un amistoso, la Federación africana ha accedido a la petición del Atlético de liberar a su futbolista, con lo que el atacante también completará toda la semana de entrenamientos con normalidad. Pese a que no se dejó ver por el verde y trabajó en el gimnasio, Grimaldo es otro de los esperados en esta semana, pues las molestias que le llevaron a abandonar la concentración de la selección no le impedirán unirse al grupo. Una recuperación de efectivos (Mateu Alemany también regresó al Cerro tras tomarse unas vacaciones aprovechando el parón) que continuará este martes con Hjulmand, ya concluida su participación con Dinamarca.

articles.title: El Almería prepara una sanción sin precedentes para Álex Sola tras su accidente
articles.standfirst: El club aplicará el régimen disciplinario interno después de que el futbolista estrellara su coche, abandonara el lugar del siniestro y triplicara la tasa de alcoholemia
articles.summary: El club aplicará el régimen disciplinario interno después de que el futbolista estrellara su coche, abandonara el lugar del siniestro y triplicara la tasa de alcoholemia
articles.body: La UD Almería ha decidido actuar con la máxima contundencia tras los graves acontecimientos protagonizados por Álex Sola durante la madrugada del sábado al domingo, apenas unas horas después de la victoria rojiblanca frente al Burgos. Según ha podido constatar MARCA, la entidad aplicará el régimen sancionador interno al futbolista, una decisión que desembocará en un castigo de carácter ejemplar y que no tiene precedentes desde la llegada de la actual propiedad saudí al club, aunque no hará ningún comunicado sobre dicho asunto ni especificará los detalles del mismo. El enfado dentro de la entidad es absoluto. Las fuentes consultadas por este periódico reconocen que el malestar es enorme por unos hechos que consideran incompatibles con la responsabilidad que debe asumir un futbolista profesional y con los valores que el club pretende transmitir tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego. Álex Sola se vio implicado en un accidente de tráfico después de estrellar su vehículo contra otros coches estacionados en la vía pública. Posteriormente abandonó el lugar del siniestro y, una vez localizado por los agentes, arrojó un resultado positivo de 0,76 miligramos de alcohol por litro de aire espirado, una cifra que triplica el límite permitido. La dirección del Almería entiende que la gravedad de lo sucedido exige una respuesta firme. Por ello, el expediente disciplinario culminará con una sanción que, según ha podido saber MARCA, será la más severa impuesta por el club desde el cambio de propiedad. El objetivo es lanzar un mensaje inequívoco de tolerancia cero ante un comportamiento que ha generado un profundo malestar en todos los estamentos de la entidad. En paralelo, ‘El Chiringuito’ fue más allá e informó este lunes de que el lateral será apartado de forma temporal de la dinámica del primer equipo además de imponérsele una durísima sanción económica.

articles.title: Messi’s Argentina farewell is here: Everything you need to know, when, where and how to watch his final game in India
articles.summary: Learn everything about Lionel Messi's final match for Argentina against Benin on October 6, 2026, including how to watch live in India and the significance of this farewell game in Buenos Aires.
articles.body: Lionel Messi is preparing to wear the Argentina shirt for the final time, bringing an extraordinary international career to its closing night in Buenos Aires. The setting could hardly be more fitting, with the Estadio Monumental expected to welcome a huge crowd for a farewell that brings together the teammates who helped him conquer world football and a younger generation preparing to take the team forward.Messi's final Argentina appearance comes at the MonumentalMessi will make his final appearance for Argentina against Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, October 6, with Indian viewers able to watch the match in the early hours of Wednesday, October 7.Kick-off is scheduled for 4:30 AM IST, while the game will stream live on ZEE5 in India and will not be televised live on Indian television.The farewell will bring an estimated 85,000 spectators to the Monumental, with members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families also expected to attend the occasion. Several players from that historic team will share the pitch with Messi one final time, alongside members of the emerging generation that will eventually inherit the responsibility of carrying Argentina forward.Benin, ranked 93rd in the world, will provide the opposition in what is officially an international friendly, although the occasion will carry considerably greater significance for the hosts than the result itself.Messi's international career now stands at 207 appearances and 125 goals for Argentina, making him the country's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, while his 68 assists also represent a national record.A career that eventually brought Messi everything with ArgentinaFor much of Messi's early international career, his relationship with Argentina was complicated, particularly after painful defeats in the 2014 World Cup final and the 2015 and 2016 Copa America finals.The turning point came with the 2021 Copa America, when Messi finally lifted a senior international trophy with Argentina, before adding the 2022 Finalissima and the World Cup in Qatar later that year. He then helped Argentina retain the Copa America title in 2024, completing an extraordinary run of major honours with the national team.His farewell arrives two and a half months after Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat by Spain in New Jersey, where Messi left the pitch in tears after struggling to influence the contest.Lionel Scaloni, the coach who built the side around Messi and found the supporting cast that helped Argentina finally end their long wait for major international success, will also oversee the farewell to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolás Otamendi.Midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up specifically for the Benin match, meaning Tuesday could also mark their final appearances for Argentina.Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although he has recently acknowledged that his playing career could end sooner than expected following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago.When and where can fans in India watch Messi's farewell?The Argentina-Benin friendly will take place at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, October 6, while the time difference means the match falls in the early hours of Wednesday for viewers in India.Match: Argentina vs BeninDate: Tuesday, October 6, 2026India date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026Kick-off: 4:30 AM ISTVenue: Estadio Monumental, Buenos AiresLive streaming in India: ZEE5Live television in India: No live TV broadcastThe match is expected to provide Messi with the farewell Argentina supporters have long imagined, with the players and families from the 2022 World Cup-winning team joining him for the occasion while Scaloni prepares to move into the next chapter without the captain who defined the previous one.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El delantero, de regreso en Madrid tras diez días recuperándose fuera de España, se ejercitó en solitario en Valdebebas con la intención de reaparecer el sábado ante el Villarreal
articles.summary: El delantero, de regreso en Madrid tras diez días recuperándose fuera de España, se ejercitó en solitario en Valdebebas con la intención de reaparecer el sábado ante el Villarreal
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé ya se ejercita en casa. Después de aterrizar este lunes en Madrid a las 11:16 horas, casi una hora más tarde de que la plantilla retomara el trabajo a las órdenes de Mourinho, el delantero completó por la tarde una sesión individual en la Ciudad Real Madrid, su primer entrenamiento sobre el césped de Valdebebas tras el parón. La sesión, de carácter vespertino, la realizó en solitario. Mbappé se ejercitó tanto en el interior de las instalaciones como sobre el terreno de juego, donde trabajó con y sin balón, señales de que la rodilla responde a las exigencias. El delantero continúa con su proceso de recuperación con la intención de estar disponible para el encuentro de este sábado ante el Villarreal, correspondiente a la octava jornada de Liga (21:00 horas), en el Santiago Bernabéu. El '10' llega a este punto tras diez días fuera de España. Se lesionó la rodilla izquierda el pasado 25 de septiembre, en el primer choque de Francia en el parón, y después de pasar una prueba médica en Valdebebas el día 26 quedó liberado para completar su recuperación lejos de la Ciudad Deportiva, con el permiso del club y del propio Mourinho. Y es que la lesión había hecho saltar las alarmas en el club, al tratarse de la misma rodilla que tantos problemas le causó la pasada campaña. Por aquel entonces el tratamiento no estuvo exento de polémica. El delantero buscó una segunda opinión fuera de España y pasó esos días lejos de Valdebebas, un periplo que, pese a contar con el visto bueno madridista, generó cierto runrún en torno a su figura.

articles.title: 14-0! India U17 women crush Iraq for biggest-ever win in Asian Cup qualifiers; Anushka hits five
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s U17 women’s side made a stunning start to their AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers campaign, registering their biggest-ever victory
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s U17 women’s side made a stunning start to their AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers campaign, registering their biggest-ever victory with a 14-0 demolition of Iraq at the MP Selayang Stadium in Selayang, Malaysia, on Monday.The Young Tigresses broke their previous record wins of 12-0 against the UAE in 2014 and Sri Lanka in 2018 with a ruthless attacking display that left Iraq struggling to cope for much of the contest.Anushka Kumari led the rout with five goals and was named Player of the Match, while skipper and centre-back Abhista Basnett scored twice. Silky Devi Sorokhaibam, Thandamoni Baskey, Nira Chanu Longjam, Pritika Barman, Joya and Alva Devi Senjam were also on the scoresheet.India run riot before weather interruptionIndia dominated from the opening whistle, combining ceaseless running, close marking and sharp one-touch passing to deny Iraq time and space.Joakim Alexandersson’s midfield controlled the game with neat distribution and compact positioning, while Redima Devi Chingkhamayum, Thandamoni, Silky and Alva repeatedly used the width to stretch the Iraqi defence.The pressure soon told as India raced into a commanding lead. Anushka struck twice before Silky scored twice for her first international goals. Thandamoni and Nira added one each as India went into the interval with a remarkable 7-0 lead.Anushka completed her fourth goal just two minutes after the restart, sweeping home a cross from Alva. Substitute Pritika then made it 9-0 by converting a rebound after substitute goalkeeper Asmaa Shivan Ahmed had initially denied India.The floodgates remained open, although the Iraqi goalkeeper produced a couple of good saves to prevent the margin from growing further.Then came an unexpected interruption.Play was halted after 64 minutes because of inclement weather, with lightning and thunder forcing the players off the field. The match resumed after a 30-minute stoppage.Young Tigresses break record after restartThe weather break did little to slow India down.Abhista rose highest to head home Ritu Badaik’s dipping corner from the right before Anushka added her fifth, placing the ball into the net from just outside the box.Joya then found an empty net after Pritika rounded the goalkeeper and squared the ball across the box, taking India to 12-0 and level with their previous record victory.Abhista headed in another Ritu corner to make it 13-0 and set a new benchmark for India at this age-group level.The record was extended further in added time. Yashica Haribabu’s free-kick came back off the bar before Abhista’s follow-up effort dropped into the six-yard box, allowing Alva to head home and complete the 14-0 rout.India will next face Syria on October 8 at 1pm IST before taking on hosts Malaysia on October 11 at 6:30pm IST in Group E. articles.title: Zubeldia se recupera y espera al Dépor
articles.standfirst: El central de Azkoitia ha vuelto a entrenar hoy con sus compañeros, tras casi un mes de baja por unas molestias musculares, y podría reaparecer el domingo si Matarazzo lo desea
articles.summary: El central de Azkoitia ha vuelto a entrenar hoy con sus compañeros, tras casi un mes de baja por unas molestias musculares, y podría reaparecer el domingo si Matarazzo lo desea
articles.body: La presencia de Igor Zubeldia, después de casi un mes de baja por unas molestias en el isquiotibial derecho, ha sido la gran novedad con la que la Real Sociedad ha regresado esta tarde a los entrenamientos, después de tener libre el fin de semana. El que no ha estado ha sido Héctor Fort, que ya se perdió el partido del viernes ante el Athletic. Pellegrino Matarazzo ha comenzado a preparar ya la llegada este domingo que viene del Deportivo de a Coruña, a la espera de que vayan regresando a su disciplina los hasta nueve internacionales que no ha tenido a sus órdenes durante el parón. Los primeros en volver a San Sebastián han sido Jon Mikel Aramburu y Yangel Herrera, liberados por el seleccionador de Venezuela del último encuentro para el que estaban convocados. Todo indica que en los próximos días se reincorporarán al trabajo de grupo de la Real, a la espera de que también lo hagan Mikel Oyarzabal, Jon Martín, Take Kubo, Mamadou Sarr, Job Ochieng, Orri Óskarsson y Luka Sucic. Mientras espera a esos futbolistas, Matarazzo ha tenido hoy la alegría de ver como Zubeldia volvía a ejercitarse con sus compañeros, después de perderse los últimos tres partidos antes del parón por unas molestias en su isquio derecho. Con el 5 de nuevo sobre el verde, el técnico de Nueva Jersey contará de nuevo con cinco centrales a su disposición, al añadirse a Jon Martín, Jon Pacheco, Sarr y Beitia. Con el que de momento no ha contado esta semana, como tampoco lo pudo hacer el viernes pasado contra el Athletic en la final de la 'Euskal Herria Txapela', ha sido Héctor Fort, que sigue arrastrando unas molestias en una rodilla.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd prodigy still expected to leave despite first-team photo inclusion - this is how it unfolded
articles.summary: Teenager JJ Gabriel remains registered to Man Utd after his camp put in a formal request to leave, but Sky Sports News reporter Danyal Khan explains why there is very little chance of him staying amid interest from a host of Europe's top clubs and what took place to reach this point...
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands the picture was taken on September 8, when Gabriel was still at the club and expected to feature for the first team this season.

It was just days later that Gabriel and his family then put in a formal request to leave.

Gabriel remains registered with United and Sky Sports News understands multiple attempts have been made to reconcile the situation with the 15-year-old and his family, with duty of care being a factor for such a young player, but no progress has been made.

Gabriel has attracted the interest of Europe's biggest clubs and talks have taken place between his camp and the likes of Barcelona and Real Madrid, with PSG and Bayern Munich also interested in the young attacking talent.

From United's perspective, they feel they have done all they can to show Gabriel and his family a clear pathway to their first team while also protecting his long-term development.

This involves, for example, featuring in the first-team squad photo that was released on Monday - a message he was to be involved in Michael Carrick's plans this season.

Another action they would point to is having Gabriel train with the first team for pre-season while also making his debut against Atletico Madrid in a friendly during that time.

However, Gabriel and his family would point to wanting more than the eight to nine minutes off the bench that he got in that particular game.

Gabriel's involvement in pre-season came after the 15-year-old failed to report back with the academy squad at the beginning of pre-season as expected.

The U21s arrived back at Carrington a week before the first team, and Gabriel was due back at the same time.

But his family believed it was beneath him and were of the view he should only be involved in first-team training and so pulled him out of reporting back with the U21s.

Sky Sports News also understands Gabriel had an individual development plan led by first-team coaches at the club, including the first-team's medical and performance departments - who all engaged with Gabriel and his family to ensure he was receiving the attention they felt he deserved.

However despite there being a feeling from inside the club the relationship between them and Gabriel's camp was harmonious, there was a difference in opinion over how much he would feature for the first-team at the beginning of the season.

Gabriel and his family requested the 15-year-old feature for at least 20 minutes against Sabah in the Champions League, Brighton in the FA Cup and Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25. This was all before beginning negotiations around a scholarship contract to secure his future at the club.

Gabriel was ineligible for the first-team tie against Sabah as he was not put in United's A-list. Instead he played against the Azerbaijani side in the UEFA Youth League that day instead and scored a hat-trick.

When Gabriel turns 16 - on October 6 - he would automatically be added to the club's B-list and would be eligible for matchday squads going forward - but Gabriel's family will believe that was the opportune moment for him to be involved in first-team action.

Gabriel has not trained with United since.

Club sources believe the tension between the two camps stem from Gabriel's family wanting to chase historical records and United wanting to protect his long-term development.

To this point, no club-to-club contact has been made regarding the availability of JJ Gabriel.

Sky Sports News has been told if a European club tries to lure him away through a FIFA loophole, United will consider legal action.

It is presumed from the club's perspective that the change in attitude from Gabriel's family around the Sabah game revolves around promises made from elsewhere - whether from another European club or potential representation acting on Gabriel and his family's behalf.

For now the teenager remains a Manchester United player and despite the fractured relationship, those at the club still believe they are the best place for Gabriel and his individual development.

However, it remains unlikely we will ever see Gabriel in a United shirt again, with Europe's biggest clubs circling the young star.

Sky Sports News has contacted Gabriel's family for comment.

articles.title: Skechers Football Lab o cómo sentirte futbolista profesional con 12 años
articles.standfirst: Los jóvenes seleccionados entre más de 160 aspirantes han vivido una concentración profesional en Los Ángeles de San Rafael, acompañados por Beñat San José y Dani Cárdenas
articles.summary: Los jóvenes seleccionados entre más de 160 aspirantes han vivido una concentración profesional en Los Ángeles de San Rafael, acompañados por Beñat San José y Dani Cárdenas
articles.body: Que el mundo del fútbol está en constante evolución no es ninguna noticia, para ello solo tienes que mirar cómo de una temporada a otra hay diversidad de cambios que afectan a todos los niveles y estamentos. Como tampoco es ninguna noticia que el fútbol formativo también vive una revolución en la que el mayor beneficiado es el joven futbolista que sueña con ser como sus ídolos. Para ello nace Skechers Footbal Lab, un proyecto diseñado para conectar con las nuevas generaciones de futbolistas y posicionar a la marca como un actor relevante dentro del ecosistema del fútbol formativo y de rendimiento. El proyecto nació para crear una experiencia diferencial alrededor del fútbol base que ha tenido su resultado final durante este último fin de semana en Los Ángeles de San Rafael, una ubicación ideal e idónea para que las jóvenes promesas se sintieran como profesionales ya que todo el evento se realizó en la sede de tantas y tantas concentraciones llevadas a cabo por el Atlético de Madrid. Durante tres días, medio centenar de niños y niñas convivieron como si de una concentración profesional se tratara. Durante todo este tiempo, además de trabajar todo el aspecto físico y táctico en el terreno de juego también recibieron una pequeña formación académica en la que se trataron aspectos como técnicos relacionados con el sistema de juego, hábitos y rutinas de descanso y nutrición y tampoco faltó la charla en la que se habló de todas las cualidades de las botas de fútbol de la marca. Una vez terminados los aspectos académicos puros y duros se vivió el momento más especial, las jóvenes promesas del mundo del fútbol compartieron dinámicas de entrenamiento con personalidades del mundo de las redes sociales como Gomeznawer, Cacho01 o Delantero09 para posteriormente recibir los consejos de dos figuras destacadas de LaLiga EA Sports, Beñat San José y Dani Cárdenas, entrenador y portero del Rayo Vallecano. Skechers Football Lab representa de este modo una nueva manera de conectar marca, fútbol y nuevas generaciones, apostando por el talento emergente y por la construcción de una comunidad auténtica alrededor del deporte.
