articles.title: De la Fuente: "Lamine Yamal tiene la ansiedad del genio, del talento especial"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente acaba de pasar por la sala de prensa del estadio del Hajduk Split para analizar el partido ante Croacia. En el amnbiente croata se mezcla el enorme peso por la derrota tremenda ante Inglaterra y la oportunidad de reaccionar ante la selección de los 41 partidos sin perder. Croacia: "Para mí es un equipo fantástico. Ha sido de las selecciones más importantes en los últimos años. Lo del otro día fue un accidente. Eso pasa una una vez en la vida. No es la diferencia entre Croacia e Inglaterra. Para nada. Les puede servir de motivación. Nosotros también queremos hacer un gran partido y dejar sellada la clasificación". Lamine Yamal. "Todos los jugadores quieren jugar. Luego nosotros evaluamos si es conveniente, o no. Lamine está en un fantástico momento y es un competidor nato. Está en un gran momento para mañana". Planes con Lamine y rotaciones. "Siempre hemos sacado el mejor equipo para el partido que teníamos que enfrentar. Es lo que hemos hecho durante todo este torneo. Nadie va a jugar más de 270 minutos, que serían tres partidos de los cuatro. Es lo que jugarán la mayoría Tercera seguida de Lamine Yamal: "Tiene ansiedad siempre porque quiere ser el mejor. Tiene la ansiedad del genio, del talento especial. La ansiedad no tiene un sentido peyorativo. Tenemos un equipo con un hambre excepcional porque ninguno se cansa de competir. Eso es Lamine". Los nuevos: "La clave es la calidad de los futbolistas, que están a la altura ante cualquier compromiso. Sabemos de qué jugadores podemos tirar para que todo vaya bien. Los chicos jóvenes se sienten muy cómodos y son muy bien acogidos". El calendario: "Me gusta por el carácter competitivo que tengo, pero con el tema del descanso sigo con la misma opinión. Me parece demasiado. Me gustaba más el otro formato. No somos quejicas y no ponemos excusas. Es el formato que hay y aquí no valen excusas ni quejas". "Recuerda que eres mortal": Siempre llevo a ese personaje a mi lado. El fútbol hoy te tiene aquí y mañana allí, pero estamos preparados para todo. Siempre digo que desdramatizo las derrotas porque en el fútbol se pierde más que se gana. Ahora es más difícil por la racha, pero todo llega. Y cuando llegue estaremos preparados. Pero siempre con los pies en el suelo". Mikel Merino: "Lleva conmigo toda la vida. Hemos vivido de todos los colores y siempre ha sido muy importante. No es más importante el futbolista que empieza el partido desde el minuto uno que el que sale en el 60. Para mí todos los jugadores son importantes. Mikel es un valor seguro salga cuando salga. ¿Podría jugar desde el inicio? Sí, pero en esos minutos nos da muchísimo. Lo importante es estar siempre preparado". Dani Olmo: "Él sabe perfectamente que es muy importante. Se adapta muy bien a los tiempos del encuentro. Lo que valoro son los momentos puntuales de cada jugador. Esta noche valoraremos en qué momento es más interesante que Dani esté en el partido, pero está con una motivación especial y es un jugador muy querido en Croacia". El nivel de España: "Hemos querido dar continuidad a una generación de futbolistas que conocíamos desde hace muchas categorías. Eso nos ha hecho ser un grupo sólido y humano con talento futbolístico. Lo han ganado todo hasta llegar a la absoluta. Ahora también vienen grandes generaciones. Ahora disfrutaremos de los que tenemos y cuando terminen ya llegarán otros. Y otro seleccionador..." Ambiente: "Nos gustan los ambientes encendidos y apasionados. Seguro que será un ambiente así. Croacia estará muy motivada, pero España también. Será un espectáculo muy bonito con un ambiente fantástico. Siempre me gusta sentir el calor del público. Ya sea a favor o en contra"

articles.title: Messi didn’t want to play in his farewell, suspects AFA is using last game to earn millions in his name: Reports
articles.summary: Lionel Messi questions the true purpose of his farewell match for Argentina, suspecting the AFA is leveraging his departure for financial gain. Reports indicate he was reluctant about the tribute match against Benin due to potential money-making motives behind it.
articles.body: Lionel Messi is about to play the final Argentina match of his career, but the farewell was reportedly not something he immediately welcomed. The occasion was always going to carry enormous significance after more than two decades with the national team, yet there was another issue behind the scenes, with Messi said to have questioned whether the match was really about saying goodbye or simply about making money from his name.Messi reportedly had doubts over the farewell matchMessi will play his 208th and final senior international for Argentina against Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, October 6, with the match beginning at 4:30 AM IST on Wednesday for viewers in India.The 39-year-old decided to end his Argentina career after the team's 2026 World Cup final defeat by Spain in New Jersey, where Messi left the pitch in tears after failing to make the influence he had hoped for in the match.His decision came during an already difficult period following his father's illness and subsequent death, with Messi acknowledging that ending his international career was a painful choice after everything he had given to Argentina.“I swear to you that I always gave it my all – not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” Messi said when announcing his retirement.According to Gazzetta dello Sport, however, Messi was initially reluctant to accept the idea of a farewell friendly against Benin because he believed the Argentine Football Association could be using the occasion to generate substantial revenue from his legacy.“Messi himself was not keen on the idea of this tribute match, as he viewed it as a final money-making venture by the AFA, using his name to secure millions in revenue,” Gazzetta reportedThe report also noted that Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni had voiced some scepticism about the farewell, suggesting that he too had doubts over how the occasion was being put together.Messi ultimately agreed to play, although the match has continued to attract controversy around the way the fixture came together.The AFA reportedly looked for opponents who would not demand a feeArgentina's extended international break included three planned home friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin, with the latter agreeing to become Messi's farewell opponent.“Benin has agreed to participate for free in Messi's farewell, content with merely appearing in a historic photograph.”The outlet also claimed that Benin's usual asking price would have been significant, while the AFA had tasked a Colombian agency with finding friendly opponents who would not demand a fee.The circumstances have added an unusual business element to what should otherwise be one of the most emotional nights in Argentine football, particularly with around 85,000 spectators expected at the Monumental.Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families will attend the farewell, joining Messi alongside members of the country's emerging generation as the national team begins life beyond its longest-serving modern captain.Lionel Scaloni, who built the Argentina side around Messi and helped deliver the country's biggest successes, will also oversee a farewell for 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolás Otamendi.Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were also called up specifically for the Benin match, raising the possibility that the game could become their final Argentina appearances as well.Messi leaves Argentina with numbers and trophies few can matchMessi's departure will close an international career that already places him among the most decorated players in Argentina's history, with a World Cup, two Copa America titles and the Finalissima among his major honours.He currently holds Argentina's records for appearances, goals and assists, having entered the farewell with 207 senior caps, 125 goals and 68 assists.His 125 goals leave him 69 ahead of Gabriel Batistuta, Argentina's second-highest goalscorer, while his 207 appearances leave him 61 ahead of Javier Mascherano.Messi will also leave Argentina as one of only four players to have made more than 200 senior international appearances, although Luka Modrić is expected to overtake him on the all-time list.Unlike Modrić and Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi leaves with a World Cup title alongside two Copa America victories, while Ronaldo's Portugal have won one European Championship during his international career.Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although he has acknowledged that his playing career could end sooner than expected following his father's death two months ago.Whatever happens after Tuesday night, Argentina's final match with Messi as captain will bring together the players who helped him finally win everything with the national team and the next generation preparing to take his place. articles.title: 8 de octubre, nuevo día clave para el futuro de Rakan Al-Thani
articles.standfirst: El hijo del jeque prestará declaración en Málaga
articles.summary: El hijo del jeque prestará declaración en Málaga
articles.body: El caso Rakan Al-Thani afronta este jueves 8 de octubre una jornada decisiva. Según ha podido saber Radio MARCA Málaga, el Juzgado de Instrucción número 14 de Málaga ha convocado a las partes y al Ministerio Fiscal a una comparecencia que tendrá lugar a las 17:00 horas por videoconferencia, después de recibir la comunicación oficial sobre la puesta a disposición de la Justicia española del hijo de Abdullah Al-Thani. Rakan Al-Thani fue detenido el pasado 12 de septiembre en el aeropuerto de Múnich, cuando se disponía a viajar a Doha. Tras su arresto, se puso en marcha la correspondiente orden europea de detención y entrega y, finalmente, un tribunal alemán dio luz verde a su traslado a España. La comparecencia de este jueves será clave para decidir qué medidas se adoptan sobre la situación personal de Rakan. Radio MARCA Málaga ha podido conocer que la Asociación de Pequeños Accionistas del Málaga CF (APA), personada en la causa, reclamará a través de sus abogados prisión provisional, comunicada y sin fianza, al considerar que existe riesgo de fuga. La entidad entiende que el intento de abandonar Alemania con destino a Doha refuerza ese argumento. Su arresto supuso además un punto de inflexión en una causa que llevaba años condicionada por la ausencia de los miembros de la familia Al-Thani ante la Justicia española. Rakan se convierte en el primer integrante de la familia puesto a disposición de los tribunales españoles desde que se activaron las órdenes de búsqueda y detención. Ahora será la jueza María de los Ángeles Ruiz González quien tenga que decidir su futuro inmediato. La celebración de la comparecencia no implica que el ingreso en prisión esté acordado de antemano. La magistrada deberá valorar las diferentes opciones existentes y determinar las medidas que considere oportunas. Una decisión con especial trascendencia para un procedimiento que investiga la gestión del Málaga CF y que, después de varios años prácticamente paralizado por la falta de comparecencia de los investigados, entra en una fase especialmente relevante.

articles.summary: Participó en Vigo en las Jornadas Nacionales de Periodismo y Deporte
articles.body: El presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas, estuvo este lunes en Vigo participando en las Jornadas Nacionales de Periodismo y Deporte, organizada por AGAXORDE, estuvo acompañado por el alcalde de la ciudad, Abel Caballero, y la presidenta del Celta, Marián Mouriño. Comenzó refiriéndose al impacto de un club profesional en una ciudad: “Un equipo representa a la ciudad y si luego tiene instalaciones, como las que ahora tiene el Celta de Vigo, todavía aumenta mucho más la pertenencia y el sentido extraordinario que los ciudadanos tengan como estandarte a su equipo. En el momento en el que vivimos es muy importante el sentido de pertenencia y a querer lo tuyo y los equipos cada día lo consiguen más. No hay ningún vigués que no se sienta orgulloso del estadio que se está haciendo”. También valoró el crecimiento del club vigués: “El Celta está en un paso de gigante los 3-4 últimos años para construir un Celta para muchos años. Lo que se necesita hoy para ser competitivo”. Y defendió LaLiga: “Somos la mejor liga del mundo y a la vista están los resultados, nuestra selección nacional o que en la final del Mundial 26 de 52 jugadores estaban en nuestra liga. Esos son los datos objetivos”. Sin necesidad de hacer muchos fichajes: “Nuestro fútbol se ha caracterizado, como hace el Celta de Vigo, por trabajar la cantera. Por eso derrochamos menos que la Premier. Nuestra Primera división es la liga de Europa en la que más minutos juegan futbolistas de la cantera”. Y se refirió a la Premier: “La liga que más dinero pierde del mundo es la Premier League. Llevan 12 mil millones de euros perdidos los 10 últimos años. Nuestros clubes son sostenibles”.

articles.title: Is Harry Kane England's greatest international?
articles.summary: With Harry Kane set to equal Peter Shilton's all-time England appearance record, where does he rank among England greats?
articles.body:
Harry Kane will write another chapter in his illustrious England history by equalling Peter Shilton's record tally of 125 caps if he plays a part in the Uefa Nations League meeting with the Czech Republic at Wembley.

England's captain is already his country's record scorer with 89 goals in 124 appearances in a full international career he started by opening his account 79 seconds into his debut.

Since that 4-0 win against Lithuania at Wembley in March 2015, he has been England's mainstay. He is still irreplaceable at 33 and their top scorer in major tournaments with 21 goals in 36 appearances across six of those showpieces, ahead of Gary Lineker's 10 goals in 18 appearances.

He is in the process of building a monument to his goalscoring brilliance at elite level as he currently stands 36 goals ahead of England's second-highest scorer Wayne Rooney, who boasts a record of 53 goals in 120 games.

Kane is unquestionably England men's most important and influential player of the modern era. The only blemish on his magnificent career is the failure – not his alone it must be stressed – to add to the one men's World Cup won in 1966.

Irrespective of that space for silverware on his CV, how highly does Kane rank in the pantheon of greats who have represented the England men's team? Could he even be the greatest? He has made himself a serious contender.

The great number nine decline - where have England's strikers gone?

Can Kane buck history and win Ballon d'Or?

Moore? Charlton? Rooney? - where does Kane rank?

This argument will instantly cut away from Kane to Bobby Moore, the elegant, unflappable defender who remains the only England captain to lift the World Cup, leading his team to triumph at Wembley in July 1966 as West Germany were beaten 4-2.

Moore was only 25 at the time, and had enjoyed success at club level with West Ham United, winning the FA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup before the World Cup. He won 108 caps between May 1962 and November 1973.

And then, of course, the conversation must turn to Sir Bobby Charlton, who survived the Munich Air Disaster with Manchester United in 1958 to become arguably England's most famous footballer of his era.

Charlton was a global beacon of dignity and world-class ability, winning the World Cup then, two years later, captaining Manchester United when they became the first English team to win the European Cup, scoring twice as Benfica were beaten 4-1 at Wembley.

He remains third on England's list of scorers, with 49 goals in 106 games.

Sir Geoff Hurst will always claim a special place with his hat-trick in the World Cup final win, while many others will have their supporters from recent times, including the likes of Wayne Rooney and David Beckham.

Former England midfielder Danny Murphy, said: "Bobby Moore will always be in people's conversation. Sir Bobby Charlton also, because of what they did and the memories they created.

"As you move forward, for me as a kid Gazza [Paul Gascoigne] burst on the scene and became a hero, especially as a creative midfield player myself.

"I think Rooney was arguably the most all-round footballer we have ever had, the most talented I've seen – but no-one can argue with Harry Kane's quality, numbers and longevity. It is the record of an England great."

He added: "There is one thing there is no debate about. Harry Kane is England's greatest goalscorer.

"No-one can take that away from him. The numbers over such a period of longevity are incredible. This, in itself, deserves all the accolades in the world. To stay at that level and not have anybody displace him is testimony to his ability and professionalism.

"He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career.

"Is he England's greatest player? This is all about opinions and eras, but his record and longevity alone informs you that he is an England great. He is in that elite group."

'We are guilty of underestimating what is in front of us'

Kane's status as an England great is beyond question. Where he stands in that list of greats will be shaped by eras and opinions, according to former internationals Paul Robinson and Murphy.

Robinson told BBC Sport that the scale of Kane's greatness may only be fully appreciated in years to come.

He said: "Harry Kane is an England great. There is no argument. He will always be part of that conversation now.

"I think we are guilty in the modern era of underestimating what we've got in front of us. We are quite happy to look through rose-tinted spectacles at what we had in the past.

"We will talk about Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton, but football now is a completely different game. The life of a footballer is completely different and it's almost like they are playing a different game.

"What Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton achieved, nobody in an England shirt has done since. You respect what they did in the era, and the status and legacy that comes with winning the World Cup and everything else they did, but we must also say it is a different game now."

Kane's double in Saturday's 7-0 win in Croatia took his tally to 11 goals in 12 games for England in this calendar year. He has also scored in six consecutive England away games, with only Sir Tom Finney having a longer run, seven between September 1946 and May 1948.

Last season alone, Ballon d'Or contender Kane scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for England and his club Bayern Munich.

He has scored five hat-tricks in an England career which includes 110 starts, with a 66% win rate.

"The biggest compliment you can pay Harry Kane is to ask yourself how long we've been pondering the question 'what will England do if Harry Kane gets injured?'," Robinson added.

"There is no-one close to his class in that position. It is taken as read the captain is playing and without the captain, we would be in trouble.

"I think we'll appreciate him even more in another 10,15, 20 years when you look back and see what he has achieved. People will point to the lack of silverware with England, but he can't play everywhere can he?

"We look back with nostalgia and fondness, saying we've had this great and that great – and England have – but make no mistake Kane is right in that debate and will be for years to come."

'The big moments haven't yet happened for him'

Kane's lack of a major international trophy will undoubtedly be the argument used to counter suggestions he is England's greatest.

He has come close, only to lose two World Cup semi-finals and two European Championship finals.

The next Euros in the United Kingdom and Ireland in 2028 could be his last chance to change that unwanted record.

Murphy, said: "The only thing really missing from him is the icing on the cake, namely getting over the line in a major tournament, which is looking less likely for him as the years go by.

"I suppose that will always be one criticism of him, as well as many England players and generations. Nobody has managed to get them over the line since 1966, and the responsibility usually does fall on the strikers or the captain.

"He didn't score in the World Cup semi-final against Croatia 2018 or in the Euros final against Italy at Wembley. He missed a penalty against France in the World Cup quarter-final in 2022, then obviously he didn't score in the Euro 2024 final against Spain or the World Cup semi-final against Argentina.

"People will look at that and say in the big moments, it didn't happen for him.

"I don't adhere to that observation at all because it's not just him and he did so much to get England in those positions. Anyone can miss a penalty. The reality is the team itself, the tactics, all those things factor into why England haven't got over the line."

As Kane stands on the brink of equalling the England caps record, he still has time – and the enduring quality - to state his case as an all-time great even more forcefully in the future.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: No reconciliation in sight for rift with Manchester United
articles.summary: As he prepares to celebrate his 16th birthday, the rift between Manchester United and JJ Gabriel shows no sign of being healed.
articles.body:
JJ Gabriel has been included in Manchester United's official team photo for this season but there remains no hint of a reconciliation with the club as new details of his efforts to leave Old Trafford emerge.

The teenage forward - who turns 16 on Tuesday - features in the photographs that were released on Monday.

It is understood the pictures were taken on 8 September - two days before he played his final game for the club and informed them of his intention to leave.

It is virtually certain his next involvement in a United game will be as an opposition player.

United still hold his registration and, according to sources close to Old Trafford, the club have made multiple attempts to reconcile the situation as part of their duty of care to the teenager. So far, it has been to no avail.

Gabriel is now a target for several of Europe's top clubs, with Real Madrid and Barcelona among those taking a keen interest. He now has a European Union passport, which is thought could smooth his passage to the continent.

However, while no clubs have approached United so far, they would consider legal action if any evidence of an illegal inducement by a club or agent - that would contravene regulations in relation to young players - was to emerge.

While tensions between Gabriel's camp and United had been simmering for a number of months, sources have told BBC Sport the player's decision to seek a move away was ultimately triggered by his non-inclusion in Michael Carrick’s side for the Champions League encounter with Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK on 10 September.

The youngster's camp had expressed a desire for Gabriel to be used as a substitute against Sabah - which, on paper, was the easiest of United's league-phase games.

Sources say the prospect of the Londoner coming on against Brighton in the EFL Cup on 16 September was also discussed, with United officials subsequently insistent that was the plan.

Had he played in either match, Gabriel would have become United's youngest ever player.

However, by the time the encounter with Fabian Hurzeler's side arrived, the striker had already told the club of his intention to quit and had left the country.

Gabriel could not play against Sabah because he had not been registered on United's Uefa A list of players when it was announced on 3 September. The precise reasons for this have not been made clear.

It did not prevent him scoring a hat-trick in a Uefa Youth League game against them at Leigh Sports Village earlier on 10 September. While he has not been back to United since, it is not clear whether anything significant happened after that game.

For their part, United believe they made it clear they view Gabriel as immensely important to their first-team future, even though sources have indicated the player did not report for the start of the academy's pre-season training schedule at the beginning of July - a week earlier than the senior squad - despite being asked to do so.

Sources also say they lobbied the Premier League to allow the forward to use "JJ Gabriel" on the back of his shirt - which they believe underlined their commitment to the academy prospect.

Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill - but he is reported to have changed his name for commercial purposes.

In addition, United say they have provided Gabriel with first-team care and services - included regular meetings with senior coaches and nutritionists.

That he was included in the senior team photo is also viewed as further evidence of their commitment to his development and transition into first-team football.

When Gabriel committed himself to United in the summer of 2025, the lure of breaking through at United, and the targets he could aim for, was strong.

He was only 14 at the time but already he was looking towards the first team. Within a couple of months, Gabriel was called into senior training sessions by Ruben Amorim.

Expectation grew to such an extent that interim boss Darren Fletcher was asked if it was possible the forward could make his competitive bow in the FA Cup third-round tie with Brighton in January.

Fletcher - then Gabriel's coach at under-18 level - said no, believing the youngster wasn't physically ready.

However, as he continued to excel at under-18 level, it seemed a case of when, not if, Gabriel would be given his chance.

He ended the 2025-26 campaign as the Premier League's Under-18 player of the year and picked up the same award at United. It seemed certain he would be involved at the start of pre-season, when the majority of United's senior players would be absent after their World Cup exertions.

What happened instead solidified existing doubts of those close to Gabriel that United were the right club for him.

First, he was not part of Carrick's squad for the trip to Helsinki to face Wrexham in a friendly. On 24 July, he was an unused substitute against Rosenborg in Trondheim, a match in which Carrick made 10 outfield changes. Five of those players have since been sold or loaned out.

Gabriel finally got his chance against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on 1 August, when he replaced Bryan Mbeumo for the final eight minutes.

That turned out to be it. He was on the bench for the final two games against Leeds and AC Milan, but did not get on. Against Leeds, former FA Youth Cup team-mate Dan Armer and 18-year-old newcomer Tynan Thompson were both introduced.

Ready or not? Why wasn't Gabriel registered for Champions League bow?

Doubts over Gabriel's physicality persisted, but his performances at under-21 level made a compelling argument he was ready.

Brighton was mentioned as a potential senior debut, but the perils around that made, for those close to Gabriel, the Champions League encounter with Sabah a better option.

The theory was correct. United beat them 4-0 and Carrick had used all five substitutes by the 72nd minute. The following week, United threw away a 2-0 lead and lost against Brighton.

Manuel Ugarte took one of the 25 spots on United's Uefa A list, even though he will not have recovered from his knee injury until after the point the squad is resubmitted for the knockout phase. Thompson was also named, as he had to be if he is to have any involvement as he is not 'home-grown'.

As he will be 16, Gabriel could have been put on the B list for all remaining seven league-phase matches. For the Sabah one, he had to take an A list spot.

Now Gabriel is in Spain, working full-time with highly respected coach Jack Hunter.

The pair have been working together since the summer of 2025 and have developed an excellent rapport. Hunter is credited with being a major influence around Gabriel having a stellar 2025-26 campaign.

It is not anticipated a final decision on Gabriel's future will be confirmed for a few weeks, with United clearly watching the situation closely.

The club has been stung by the chain of events and believe they have done all they could to avoid it.

The player's side have a different view.

There has been criticism of the way Gabriel's future has been handled, largely due to United's track record in bringing young players though and giving them a chance.

However, those closest to the player are certain the path they are taking is the right one.

articles.title: Liverpool: Andoni Iraola's early impact at Anfield assessed ahead of huge Super Sunday showdown with Man City
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola's start at Liverpool examined on the Sky Sports Premier League Podcast; Have big selection calls and pragmatic moves set up opportunity for high-octane lift-off this weekend? Watch Liverpool vs Man City live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm.
articles.body:
The impact of the new Reds boss is assessed in the latest Sky Sports Premier League podcast.

Peter Smith is joined by reporters Vinny O'Connor and Mark McAdam , and writer Dan Morgan to pick over the standout tactical ideas Iraola has brought to Liverpool so far and weigh up the impact of summer signings on the balance of the squad.

They also preview the hotly-anticipated showdown with City, which could prove to be a decisive moment at the start of Iraola's reign…

"What I've seen from Andoni Iraola is that he's happy to make big decisions - and it was a big decision to leave out Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araujo at right-back and it's worked. Liverpool needed to be more solid; they've done that

"Leaving Ryan Gravenberch out, for instance, as well. Iraola has taken that decision. When he's decided to use the youngsters - Lewis Koumas, playing him up front; when he's brought in Trey Nyoni. It seems he's given the trust to the youngsters and that's a real big plus.

"It's not all been perfect but we're gradually beginning to see Iraola's influence with the press. Teams aren't able to settle on the ball as much as they would like to against Liverpool, they're not allowing teams as many passes.

"Yes, at times they've still been caught on the break and that's an area for improvement and I think he's still trying to strive for that ideal balance in midfield.

"But with those three clean sheets in the Premier League in the last three games we're seeing a team that defends the box a lot better, and when they've got the ball, they're getting the ball forward quicker and creating chances, which bodes well for the future.

"We're seeing the signs that it's going to get that little bit more exciting and I don't think we're too far away from seeing more regular high octane football under him."

'Atletico Madrid win showed Iraola can beat big hitters'

"The key thing is they're unbeaten. When you go into a new football club, don't lose games! But that big win in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid is a massive plus because not only does that show that they can win games but they can do it against the big teams, the big hitters, those sides that are going to challenge them.

"I've been really impressed so far. There's been a transition period and the key thing that Andoni will need - and what he had at Bournemouth - was time. Time on the training pitch, time to work with the players, time to understand the players.

"It certainly feels like he's very conscious that you need to be defensively solid and you need to have more of the ball [at Liverpool].

"But I said in the summer, if I could have a season ticket to follow Liverpool around for the first six months of Andoni Iraola's term I would absolutely do it because when he is at it and at his very best there's no question it will be one of the most exciting brands of football that Liverpool fans have seen for some time.

"I know they'll go 'well, Jurgen Klopp was the manager not that long ago!' But it will hopefully be something that is very similar to that style of football."

Liverpool podcaster and writer Dan Morgan:

"In general, I'd say quietly impressive. He surprised me in the sense that I thought idealistically, in terms of how his Bournemouth teams played, I thought his philosophy was going to be something that he was going to be wedded to unconditionally. You play his way, it's relentless, real high-octane energy stuff.

"But he's done things that I think other Liverpool managers in the past would have done. For example, Rafa Benitez would have maybe seen the need to use a centre-back at right back just to shore up Liverpool's issues defensively, especially around set-pieces. Iraola has done that with Ronaldo Araujo. Similarly, Jurgen Klopp would have looked at someone like Lewis Koumas and said, 'I can do something with this young player, he's sticking around'.

"I think that speaks to him recognising the size of the job. He was aware that he can't go 10 games without a win in his first 10 Liverpool games - that would just bring on too much pressure and too much noise - so he's found a way to quietly get results.

"But from a Liverpool supporter, I think there is still that anticipation of, 'OK, when is the big moment going to arrive?' And there's a big opportunity on Sunday…"

articles.title: La donación de Dani Olmo a Vukovar que acabó con una sentida ovación de los periodistas croatas
articles.standfirst: El futbolista dona el 2% de su sueldo desde que se fue del país.
articles.summary: El futbolista dona el 2% de su sueldo desde que se fue del país.
articles.body: El representante de Dani Olmo, Andy Bara, reveló hace unos días en el podcast Inkubator un aspecto solidario que casi nadie conocía de la vida del futbolista: "Desde que dejó el Dinamo, ha estado donando el 2% de su salario bruto anual al Vukovar. Son cantidades importantes porque gana muchísimo dinero y esto viene ocurriendo desde que estaba en Leipzig y ahora en Barcelona. No habla de ello públicamente, pero quiero decirlo porque se lo merece", explicaba. La noticia saltó a los medios croatas y en la rueda de prensa le han preguntado por ello. "No sabía que esto había salido a la luz. Cuando me fui me sentía en deuda con Croacia y quería devolverle algo, así que hemos decido hacer esa donación a las familias de Vukovar. Me sentía en deuda y creía que esto era la mejor idea", explicó. Vukovar fue una de las ciudades más afectadas por la guerra de los Balcanes. Sufrió un asedio durante 87 días por parte del Ejército Popular Yugoslavo y fuerzas paramilitares serbias entre agosto y noviembre de 1991 y sus consecuencias fueron dramáticas. Dani quiso devolver a Croacia parte de lo que la ciudad le dio cuando se marchó del Dinamo y por eso dona el 2% de su salario anual bruto cada año. En Split, los periodistas croatas aprovecharon para darle una ovación por ese gesto que está incluido en las acciones solidarias de Common Goal, de Juan Mata. La ayuda no está destinada exclusivamente a Vukovar, sino también a Slavonski Brod, donde el jugador estuvo hace unos cuatro o cinco años y quedó muy marcado por lo que vio. "Estuve allí con los chicos y jugamos un poco durante ese día. Hicimos algunas actividades relacionadas con el deporte. Sentí que tenía que darle algo a Croacia por todo lo que me había dado y pensé que hacerlo a través de Common Goal sería la mejor manera", explicó el media punta.

articles.title: ¿Qué sucedió en Vukovar, la ciudad a la que ayuda Dani Olmo?
articles.standfirst: La masacre de noviembre de 1991 es una las grandes tragedias de la guerra de los Balcanes
articles.summary: La masacre de noviembre de 1991 es una las grandes tragedias de la guerra de los Balcanes
articles.body: Hay ciudades que con solo mencionarlas se remueve la conciencia. Y los estómagos. Para los croatas, Vukovar es una de ellos. A apenas unos kilómetros de la frontera con Serbia, esta localidad a orillas del Danubio se convirtió en 1991 en el escenario de uno de los episodios más trágicos y simbólicos de la guerra que acompañó la desintegración de Yugoslavia. Esa la ciudad a la que Dani Olmo ayuda con un 2% de su salario como agradecimiento a todo lo que ha dado Croacia. Los periodistas croatas agradecieron su gesto con un aplauso en la sala de prensa del Hajduk Split. Durante 87 días, entre agosto y noviembre de 1991, Vukovar resistió el asedio del Ejército Popular Yugoslavo y de fuerzas paramilitares serbias. Lo que comenzó como una batalla por el control de una ciudad estratégica terminó transformándose en una devastación casi total. Los bombardeos arrasaron barrios enteros y la localidad quedó reducida a escombros tras uno de los asedios más duros vividos en Europa desde la II Guerra Mundial. La caída de Vukovar, el 18 de noviembre de 1991, marcó un antes y un después para Croacia. Tras la conquista llegaron las deportaciones masivas de civiles y, pocos días después, la matanza de Ovčara. Más de 200 prisioneros de guerra y civiles fueron ejecutados después de ser sacados del hospital de la ciudad, un crimen de guerra que conmocionó al continente y que aún hoy sigue siendo uno de los símbolos del sufrimiento croata durante el conflicto. Treinta y cinco años después, las cicatrices siguen visibles. Aunque Vukovar fue reintegrada pacíficamente a Croacia en 1998, su nombre continúa ocupando un lugar especial en la memoria colectiva del país. Cada aniversario de la caída de la ciudad reúne a miles de personas en actos de homenaje a las víctimas y a quienes defendieron la localidad durante aquellos meses dramáticos. La imagen más reconocible de aquella tragedia es la torre del agua de Vukovar. Alcanzada por cientos de impactos durante el asedio, fue conservada tal y como quedó al final de la guerra y se ha convertido en uno de los grandes símbolos nacionales de Croacia. Un monumento que recuerda que, para todo un país, Vukovar no es solo una ciudad: es memoria al horror que se vivió en los Balcanes.

articles.title: Premier League viewership in US up 20 percent among young Americans
articles.summary: English Premier League viewership up 20 percent among young Americans following World Cup, Nielsen Sports data shows.
articles.body:
The Premier League has struck a ⁠chord with young ⁠Americans after the US cohosted this year’s World Cup, with viewership for the English top-flight up 20 percent among ⁠18-34-year-olds so far this season, shows data from Nielsen Sports released on Monday.

US broadcasters NBC and the USA Network ⁠have attracted an average of half a million viewers for Premier League games so far this season – a 3 percent increase as the sport’s popularity has grown.

“The World Cup served as a powerful catalyst, expanding the Premier ‌League’s footprint across a far broader demographic in the US,” said Jon Stainer, global GM at Nielsen Sports.

“Our data shows that fandom is not only reaching record highs but it is also expanding rapidly among younger, diverse audiences and carrying over into major domestic and international leagues.”

articles.title: El Córdoba resurge y tumba a un indómito Tenerife a base de golazos
articles.standfirst: Los blanquiverdes tuvieron que adelantarse tres vencer para vencer en un duelo que decidió Isma Ruiz
articles.summary: Los blanquiverdes tuvieron que adelantarse tres vencer para vencer en un duelo que decidió Isma Ruiz
articles.body: El Córdoba se reencontró con la victoria en el Nuevo Arcángel ante un respondón Tenerife, que le igualó por dos veces los tantos de Eder García y Diego Percan con otros de Gomis y Ranos. Al tercero, otro golazo blanquiverde de Isma Ruiz, más de medio equipo como siempre para los locales, ya no tuvieron respuesta. Los califales salen de la zona roja, a la que habían caído con los resultados de la jornada, cortando la mala racha de dos derrotas seguidas en casa y cuatro en las anteriores cinco jornadas, mientras el Tete no levanta cabeza: un solo triunfo en los últimos seis encuentros. Los partidos del Córdoba se viven siempre en un permanente psiquiátrico. Fútbol, con sus carencias y virtudes, como si el mañana no existiera. Esta vez en veintipocos minutos el encuentro ya tenía tres tantos, cuando otros partidos entre grandes de LaLiga se van hasta el final sin abrirse. Al tercero marcó Eder García, con un trallazo desde la frontal a pase de Carracedo que golpeó en el larguero antes de entrar y que necesitó la validación del VAR; después empató Gomis que resolvió de manera magistral el uno contra uno con Guilherme tras recibir de Iván Chapela e irse en velocidad; y finalmente Percan remató a placer en el segundo palo el gran pase de Diego Bri tras una sublime combinación del equipo blanquiverde, precisa y al primer toque, para dar la segunda ventaja al equipo de Iván Ania. A partir de ahí hubo más del otro fútbol, con una acción polémica antes de la media hora. Un intento de cabezazo de Enric Gallego a Rubén Alves en un rifirrafe entre los dos acabó con roja para el central local y amarilla para el delantero visitante. Pero Rubén Ávalos avisó desde el VAR de su error a Alejandro Ojaos, que lo corrigió a medias,. porque dejó la disputa en amarilla para los dos. La intensidad del duelo dejó un buen número de amarillas hasta los 52 minutos que duró el primer acto, con reclamaciones de la segunda para Gerard Valentín y Juanjo Sánchez. Entre tanto Percan y Diego Bri tuvieron las mejores opciones en lo que fue puramente futbolístico, aunque la zaga local tuvo que multiplicarse ante las intentonas del Tenerife, sobre todo con una salvada de Tasende, que evitó el empate al sacar de cabeza casi bajo el larguero un centro que se disponía a remachar Enric Gallego. El Tenerife hizo cambios para la segunda parte, con las entradas de Nacho Gil y Dani Fernández, aunque el Córdoba fue el que tuvo las mejores ocasiones del reinicio. Hasta tres casi seguidas de Adnane Ghailan, dos de ellas bastante buenas, sobre todo una en la que parecía más fácil mandar dentro el pase de Diego Bri. El cuadro chicharrero sobrevivió y, justo cuando Iván Ania había metido a Damián Cáceres para sostener al equipo, junto a Kevin Medina, volvió a empatar el partido con un disparo cruzado de Ranos que dio en el poste antes de entrar tras un error local en la salida de balón. Pese a que Kevin Medina tuvo una buena arrancada tras el 2-2 y Percan perdonó en un cabezazo solo tras pase de Ghailan justo antes de dejar su sitio a Enol, el cuadro insular no estaba incómodo. De hecho, Dani Fernández perdonó de zurda poco antes de que Isma Ruiz, en una escaramuza de Kevin Medina, se sacara un zurdazo desde la frontal del área grande a la red chicharrera. El Córdoba, por tercera vez en ventaja, agotó cambios con las entradas de Egoitz y Theo Zidane, mientras Juanjo Sánchez se fue a los vestuarios antes de tiempo al ver su segunda amonestación en el minuto 87. Ojaos dio cinco de añadido, pero nada relevante pasó

articles.title: Italia vuelve a ganar a Turquía y continúa creciendo
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Scamacca, Calafiori y Esposito sirvieron para vencer a Turquía, que llegó a empatar con el gol de Simsir
articles.summary: Los goles de Scamacca, Calafiori y Esposito sirvieron para vencer a Turquía, que llegó a empatar con el gol de Simsir
articles.body: Turquía tenía que ganar si quería seguir con posibilidades de obrar el milagro y clasificarse. Un gigante Donnarumma y un Scamacca que sacó sus dotes de '9' complicaban la vida a los turcos. Llegaron a igualar por medio de Simsir, pero cuatro minutos después, Calafiori sacó un gran cabezazo y en los minutos finales, el toque de Esposito puso la puntilla. Italia se impuso nuevamente a los otomanos, por segunda vez en una semana. Tras siete días volvían a enfrentarse Italia y Turquía. Duelo entre técnicos italianos. Roberto Mancini con los locales y Vincenzo Montella con los visitantes. Una semana para repasar los errores cometidos en el primer encuentro y conocer las debilidades del contrario. Aunque el conjunto otomano no contaba ni con Yilmaz ni con Güler, que estaban sancionados por acumulación de tarjetas. Italia comenzó con el balón, pero con el paso de los minutos, Turquía comenzó a crecerse, encerrando a los locales y probando en varias ocasiones la meta de la 'Azzurra'. Sin embargo, Donnarumma salvó la portería. Ese acoso de los visitantes, hizo que los locales fuesen abucheados por su propio público. Esa confianza de Turquía se vendría abajo con el tanto de Scamacca. Centro lateral, Doumbia fue a pelearla y el rechace cayó en los pies del '11'. El delantero italiano la enganchó a bote pronto y mandó el balón al fondo de la red tras tocar el larguero. La segunda parte comenzó con ocasiones para los dos bandos. Aunque la más clara fue para Italia. Esposito cedió un gran balón para Doumbia que se quedó ante Çakir. Pero el meta se mantuvo firma y sacó un gran pie para evitar que la diferencia de goles creciese. Esa acción iba a volver a generar la confianza que Turquía había perdido en la primera parte. Pasados 15 minutos Celik recibió el balón en línea de fondo y lo centró al corazón del área con un pase raso. Elmali tocó de tacón y Simsir estaba en el segundo palo para empujar el balón y poner el empate. Sin embargo, la alegría no duraría mucho. Apenas tres minutos después, Elmali cometió una falta lateral. En el centro de Barella, Calafiori le ganó la partida al futbolista que cometió la falta y con un gran remate, Italia se volvió a adelantar. Italia buscaba el tercero para finiquitar el partido, pero no llegaba. Donnarumma tuvo que aparecer para palmear un disparo de Ozcan desde la frontal para mantener la ventaja. Sin embargo, la fragilidad defensiva daba sensaciones de que en cualquier momento podía llegar el empate. Pero terminó llegando el tercero. Error en la salida de balón. Doumbia recuperó, pero su disparó lo despejó Kadioglu. El rechace le cayó a Romano que realizó un centrochut directo hacia Esposito. El delantero con un toque puso el tercero para la 'Azzurra' e Italia le ganó a Turquía el segundo partido en siete días.

articles.title: Olise le regala a Zidane su primera gran noche en el Stade de France
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Bayern entró en la segunda parte y revolucionó el choque fabricando tres de los cuatro goles de la remontada contra Bélgica (4-1)
articles.summary: El extremo del Bayern entró en la segunda parte y revolucionó el choque fabricando tres de los cuatro goles de la remontada contra Bélgica (4-1)
articles.body: No quiere focos. Pero todos le apuntan de manera irremediable. Salvo uno, todos los goles de Francia en esta Nations League han llevado el sello de Olise: asistió a Mbappé ante Turquía; marcó contra Bélgica e Italia; y salió desde el banquillo para repartir la asistencia de la remontada ante los 'diablos rojos'... antes de ratificar el primer triunfo de Zidane en el Stade de France con un doblete en los últimos minutos. No le tembló el pulso a Zidane para renovar por completo el once que venía de empatar ante Italia: premió a Restes y Yoro permitiéndoles debutar; Koundé regresó tras quedarse sin minutos en los dos últimos partidos; y Camavinga acompañó a Koné y Akliouche en la medular. Van Bommel, por su parte, también introdujo hasta seis novedades. Dos de ellas, Lavia y Raskin, obligadas por las sanciones de Tielemans y De Bruyne. Con Camavinga tratando de mostrarse bastante activo para agilizar el juego intercalando alturas con Koné, Francia arrancó volcando el juego sobre un Ousmane Dembélé que, sin embargo, dejó claro en la primera acción que no estaba del todo fino. Recibió en el pico del área, desbordó hacia dentro... y mandó su disparo al córner. Barcola, por el sector opuesto, sí parecía tener mucha más 'chispa'. Sin apenas esfuerzo, dejó atrás a Castagne en las dos primeras acciones que tuvo la oportunidad de encarar. Estuvo atento Vandeevordt, que se estrenaba con Bélgica, para achicharle en un mano mano. Antes, eso sí, fue Lukaku quien se contabilizó el primer remate a puerta del partido tras pivotar sobre Lacroix. Se reclamó con insistencia un penalti por mano de Lukebakio cuando todavía no se había llegado a la hora de partido. Poco después, sin embargo, el ex del Sevilla silenció Saint-Denis. Lavia, que estaba realizando un gran partido interceptando balones, levantó la cabeza en la corona de su propia área y, sin oposición, puso a correr al extremo del Benfica... y éste resolvió de maravilla ante Restes. Le estaba faltando creatividad a Francia. Pero, a partir de entonces, la realidad es que el colapso fue total. De hecho, ni siquiera volvieron a probar un disparo antes de marcharse al descanso. No introdujo ningún cambio Zidane al descanso. Pero la conversación que tuvo con Koné y Camavinga antes de afrontar la segunda parte fue reveladora. Francia trató de subir marchas y comenzó a probar desde larga distancia. Pero, justo en el momento que se cumplió la hora de partido, 'Zizou' llamó a filas a Da Cunha, Cherki y Olise con la clara intención de incorporar más sensibilidad en la distribución, desborde y, sobre todo, imaginación en los últimos metros. El impacto fue manifiesto y, en cuestión de tres minutos, Francia le dio la vuelta al partido. Da Cunha habilitó el 1-1 transformado por un Désiré Doué —acababa de entrar por Barcola— que batió a Vandervoordt con la zurda tras darse la vuelta en el balcón del área y, acto seguido, Olise desbordó por derecha para servir el tanto de la remontada convertido por Cherki llegando desde atrás. El trabajo ya estaba hecho... pero Olise decidió darse un festín transformando un doblete, ambos a pase de Doué, para redondear otra actuación sobresaliente: ya son 23 goles en 29 partidos con Francia; 17 en lo que marcha de 2026 y 13 desde el Mundial. No es un momento de forma puntual. Es uno de los mejores jugadores del planeta. Normal que Zidane no pudiese contener su sonrisa.

articles.title: College football has never been more chaotic — and its fans are losing their minds because of it
articles.summary: A certain level of off-the-wall bizarre gives college football its charm. But why does it seem this season like it's driving everyone up the wall?
articles.body:
Just one week ago, coming off a dominant victory over Ole Miss to reach 4-0, it would have been difficult to find a Florida fan who felt anything but elation over first-year coach Jon Sumrall.

But by Saturday night, the tables had turned on the Gators in a 45-17 loss at Missouri , and the online discourse around Sumrall had quickly turned toxic.

"There better be staff changes Day 1 of offseason," one verified Florida fan account with more than 1,000 followers posted on X. Another with 2,000 followers, whose account was subsequently suspended, made a profane critique of Sumrall for going on a podcast tour after the Ole Miss win and not having his team ready to play. On a popular Gators message board, there were separate threads calling for the firing of defensive coordinator Brad White and mega-booster Gary Condron as well as one calling Sumrall a "fraud."

While overheated social media rhetoric is a feature and not a bug of college football fandom, it does feel like the first half of the 2026 season has been defined by more emotional volatility and less patience than ever before.

Whether it's a group of TCU fans wearing paper bags this past week against BYU to protest head coach Sonny Dykes, Florida State coach Mike Norvell being booed during the introductions before a big win over Virginia or Arkansas fans openly speculating whether first-year coach Ryan Silverfield might be one-and-done, a sport that is supposed to provide joy and community seems at the moment to instead be a source of frustration in so many places.

While the online conversation only represents the most fervent sliver of every fan base, the atmosphere around college football feels like it is getting progressively more intense and more toxic. It's not just the fans, either. Administrators are feeling the stress of one bad football season putting their jobs in jeopardy. Coaches' capacity for patience is getting squeezed, too — just look at the sideline blowup at Colorado State last weekend between Jim Mora and defensive coordinator Tyson Summers, who walked off the job mid-game after getting stripped of his play-calling duties .

A certain level of bizarre makes college football what it is. But why does it seem this season like it's driving everyone up the wall?

The answer lies within the vast realm of one word: Disruption.

Just think about the amount of change college football has endured within a short period of time.

Players went from not being paid to making, in some cases, millions of dollars annually, spreading the talent around in ways that weren't happening under the old model.

The concept of team building went from developing multiple recruiting classes over the course of several years to a plug-and-play model where relying too much on prospects, even elite ones, can be a disadvantage.

Fans and administrators used to judge coaches partly on their ability to attract talent, even if it meant overlooking deficiencies in their strategic and technical prowess. Now, it seems the only meaningful measure of building a roster is money, meaning schools that aren't winning have to ask their fans for more of it at the very moment their frustration with the product is highest.

Conferences completely remade themselves, with the SEC absorbing two more historic powers in Texas and Oklahoma and the Big Ten adding the best programs from the West Coast, making both leagues more difficult to win and also more uneven from a scheduling standpoint.

The playoff has gone from four teams to 12, and now possibly to 24 as soon as next season, which is great for college football in some ways but has pretty much eliminated the entire paradigm of schools achieving something important by making a bowl game. Meanwhile, more and more players are opting out of the bowls, which are slowly dying off and could be reimagined or killed entirely with more playoff expansion.

Oh, and Indiana — one of the worst power conference programs for the last several decades — created an impossible standard for every school mired in mediocrity by winning a national championship two years after it hired Curt Cignetti.

All of that happened within the last five years. You cannot turn a sport on its head to this extent, within such a short window of time, and expect people to instantly adjust the way they've processed college football their entire lives. It's just too much.

Many of these developments represent progress for a sport that used to move at a glacial pace, but everything comes with trade-offs. And sometimes those of us in the media, particularly the college football-focused media, are too quick to dismiss the concerns of those who see cracks in the foundation because TV ratings are still very good and many stadiums are full.

College football is resilient, but it's not immune from a market correction if the sport's leadership overreaches or moves too quickly for its fans to process. Every action will lead to consequences, even if they're unintended and in some cases undesirable.

On one hand, the unfettered NIL/transfer market has led to more parity between, say, a traditional power like Alabama and a historically middle class program like Ole Miss. That's a positive development for a sport where the elite talent used to cluster at a small number of schools.

At this moment, there are at least 10 teams that have every right to believe they can win a national championship this season and another 10 that could convince themselves they're on the verge of doing it in the next year or two if they hit on a couple players in the transfer portal. That never used to be the case in college football.

But there are downsides, too. When nobody is that much better than anybody else and there is little continuity with a roster from year to year, inconsistency like we saw at Florida from last week to this week will become the norm. It's an NFL-style setup for a sport that in many ways is still rooted in the BCS-era mentality that perfection is the best measure of excellence.

Meanwhile, fans of programs outside the power conferences are feeling the pain differently because their rosters are getting ransacked every year by programs that can spend more to poach their players. The old days where a Boise State could establish its national brand by beating Oklahoma in the 2007 Fiesta Bowl or UCF celebrating an unbeaten season probably won't happen again.

A great example of how this is playing out occurred at Southern Miss recently, where head coach Blake Anderson was asked how to fix his team's slow starts on offense. "Quit playing Auburn and UConn and Tulane," he said. "Playing people that look like us might be a help." That comment predictably riled up Southern Miss fans, many of whom remember an era under Jeff Bower where they would regularly play tough against ranked teams and occasionally put a major conference scalp on the wall. Though Anderson apologized and tried to clarify what he meant, he was simply being honest about what will happen most of the time when Southern Miss plays a school that invested significantly more money into its roster.

Whether you're Southern Miss in the Sun Belt or Arkansas in the SEC — another school whose fan base is furious because it has fallen behind its competition financially — there is no easy way anymore to generate hope.

A decade ago, a school could buy out its unpopular coach and immediately see a return on that investment when the charismatic new guy got donors excited and sold a bunch of tickets. Now, as Arkansas is figuring out in real time, there is little point in hiring a new coach unless the commitment to spend more money has already been made.

In this environment, you can understand why many coaches and college administrators desperately want a 24-team playoff. If schools are forced to invest between $30-50 million in a roster just to have a chance at success, they are demanding more opportunity to have something to show for it. A trip to the Pop-Tarts Bowl, despite its enchanting quirkiness, isn't enough anymore.

But there's a problem with that theory. No matter how much schools invest, and no matter how many playoff spots are available, half the teams will lose every single weekend. Sometimes, half of the winners will be unhappy about how they won because every current adult college football fan grew up in an era where determining a national champion was almost like a beauty pageant.

In some ways, it feels like the simple act of celebrating a win with the fervor of Minnesota coach P.J. Fleck is a throwback to a different time. When he goes viral for smearing a players' blood on his face or drinking out of the Little Brown Jug after beating Michigan and crowd surfing in the locker room, nobody's talking Minnesota's NIL budget or how it impacts the playoff race. Teams like Minnesota seem to be part of fewer and fewer of those moments when it's purely about the joy of the sport.

We are seeing these changes little by little, but in some ways too quickly for our brains to adjust to the product we're watching every week.

College football has been disrupted more quickly and violently than perhaps any sport in modern times, and there's a lot of good that has come from it. But the transition from what it used to be to what it is now hasn't been perfect. It has created a different set of winners and losers, and it is producing a level of angst that fans, coaches and administrators are struggling to deal with and the media is struggling to capture in its full context.

The sport is not in crisis. It is also far from perfect. Everyone has an opinion on what college football should look like, but we all have to accept that it is changing in some ways we will like and others we will hate.

Whether we can adjust to that reality before demanding that everyone be fired remains to be seen.

articles.title: Scotland: Humble Billy Gilmour happy with new role as 50th cap beckons
articles.summary: Billy Gilmour is excited by the prospect of earning a 50th Scotland cap after a key role in Sebastien Pocognoli's first win as national head coach.
articles.body:
Still fresh-faced, still slight of stature, still to reach the peak of his powers after a career blighted by untimely injuries, it is hard to believe Billy Gilmour is already on the brink of a 50th cap for Scotland.

The 25-year-old midfielder at last is winning the regular first-team starts, not only with the national team but also with Napoli, his talent surely deserves.

His cause has, ironically, been aided in part by the absence through illness from both of clubmate Scott McTominay.

It has also certainly encouraged new national head coach Sebastien Pocognoli to urge Gilmour to take the kind of more advanced positions his fellow midfielder occupied under predecessor Steve Clarke.

More of that later, because we really should be making more of that cap landmark.

Well, we would if the man himself did not play it down as "overall, it's another game" as he prepares for a personal bit of history at home to Slovenia in Nations League Group B1 on Tuesday.

Pocognoli backs Scotland strikers for 'must-win' game against Slovenia

You are the Scotland boss - what would you do?

Bowie seizing Scotland shot after World Cup disappointment

As you might expect from someone Ayrshire born, there are no airs and graces about Gilmour.

Indeed, the biggest headline about him this week was juvenile club Ardrossan Winton Rovers naming a stand in his honour as part of his sponsorship deal with his once local club.

Gilmour does admit to "excitement" at the prospect of that 50th cap, but he stresses that his thoughts are mainly on "hopefully a good game and a win".

"I'm always so proud to put on my national team jersey and go out there," he said.

"We're very lucky as well. Not everyone gets to represent their country in sports."

Raided by Chelsea from Rangers' academy as he was about to make the Ibrox first-team aged just 16, Gilmour made his Premier League debut two years later.

His progress at Stamford Bridge hampered by a serious knee injury, he had a difficult time on loan to Norwich City before gradually finding his confidence again at Brighton & Hove Albion.

However, it is with Napoli where Gilmour, joining at the same time as McTominay arrived from Manchester United, has made his reputation.

Winning Serie A in their first season, Gilmour's progress was nevertheless again hampered by a groin problem at the turn of the year before the biggest blow yet - a knee injury picked up in the final pre-tournament friendly that ruled him out of this summer's World Cup.

"Ups and downs" is his understated description of his career so far.

"Matured a lot," he added when asked how he had changed since his first cap in 2021. "But, for me, I think I'm still the same player.

"I still want to get on the ball, get on the ball technically. I know I'm not the strongest or biggest, so I try to stay away from all that, but I try to do my best whatever I'm told to do."

What Pocognoli has told him to do is try to influence the game "higher up the pitch".

"It's nice to hear that he wants me to play in a more advanced role," Gilmour said.

"If he asks me to do a job then I'll do my best anywhere on the pitch, whether it's in defence or up front. Most of all, I'm just happy to be playing.

"I know, if I'm not on the ball, I can't be a threat as much as I want to in the game."

Gilmour set up Sassuolo striker Kieron Bowie for the first goal of Pocognoli's reign and send them on to the Belgian's first victory, 2-0 in North Macedonia on Saturday.

"As a group, you've seen we are aggressive and on the front foot, playing through the lines, and we've created a lot of chances, although we have not took as many as we'd have liked," he said when asked what had changed tactically under the new regime.

"But we're creating chances, the fans are getting excited and us, as players, we enjoy playing it.

"Of course it's still early and will take time, but we're doing well so far."

Gilmour will now be dreaming matching what he described as the "incredible" and "amazing" achievement of captain Andy Robertson, who earned his 100th cap in Skopje.

Ever humble, though, Gilmour already sees himself as one of the elder statesmen willing to pass down his advice to some of the fresh young talent being squeezed into the squad by the new head coach.

"I was the youngest when I came in," Gilmour recalled. "Steve Clarke brought me in and I can't thank him enough for putting his trust in me.

"I think we've got great players in the squad - a lot of new faces also. We have experienced players who will help the youngsters, but we'll need to take our time and be patient, but so far we're getting to grips with it."

Pocognoli has certainly seen Gilmour's value, with three starts in three games.

"We try to play the football he also likes because he is really involved in terms of the connection between the defenders and high up the pitch," the Belgian said.

"With Napoli, he just started to play some minutes before the camp, but now I hope it will help him take the next step with his club."

Slovenia counterpart Bostjan Cesar is also an admirer - and is aware of the danger posed to his side by Scotland's diminutive midfield general.

"Billy Gilmour is a very good player in the Italian top division and he had a really good season, where he was the engine of his team," he said.

articles.title: Buchanan regresa tocado y es duda para el Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El canadiense abandona la concentración de su selección por una lesión en el isquiotibial
articles.summary: El canadiense abandona la concentración de su selección por una lesión en el isquiotibial
articles.body: La fecha FIFA puede dejar su primera “víctima” en el Villarreal antes de visitar el Santiago Bernabéu. Y es que el canadiense Tajon Buchanan es seria duda para medirse al Real Madrid este sábado después de sufrir una lesión en el isquiotibial durante el último compromiso de Canadá ante Perú. El extremo amarillo, que participó en la victoria canadiense por 2-0, ha tenido que abandonar la concentración de su selección y regresar a Vila-real. Allí será sometido a las pruebas médicas que deberán determinar el alcance exacto de la lesión y sus plazos de recuperación. Buchanan no podrá participar en el próximo amistoso de Canadá frente a Estados Unidos y queda ahora pendiente de evolución. En el Villarreal cruzan los dedos para que la dolencia no revista gravedad y el internacional canadiense pueda llegar a tiempo a una de las citas más exigentes de un calendario especialmente duro como el que espera en este mes de octubre a los amarillos Su presencia en el Bernabéu queda, por tanto, en el aire a falta de conocer el resultado de las pruebas médicas. El canadiense era poco menos que un intocable en este inicio de temporada para el Villarreal.

articles.title: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule Talks Cameo on HBO's 'Lanterns' in New Video
articles.summary: College football fans who watched the season finale of HBO's Lanterns on Sunday saw a familiar face when Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule made a cameo.
articles.body:
College football fans who watched the season finale of HBO's Lanterns on Sunday saw a familiar face when Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule made a cameo.

"I don't know that I'll be taking my talents to Broadway anytime soon, but it was really cool to see Nebraska on HBO and to have a chance to do it," he told reporters Monday. "My daughters were probably more fired up than I was. They were very concerned I would not get my line right. It was a very cool experience."

He also called Lanterns a "great show" and expressed his gratitude for those who helped his cameo become a reality.

Rhule made an appearance on the show as himself recruiting an elite quarterback character at a high school football game.

The coach's appearance comes as his fourth season with Nebraska is off to an excellent start. The Cornhuskers are 5-0 overall and 2-0 in the Big Ten with conference victories over Michigan State and Maryland.

They will also have an opportunity to prove themselves on a national stage during their next two games against Indiana and Oregon.

If they win those, it will probably help Rhule's recruiting efforts both in reality and inside the DC Universe.

articles.title: De la Fuente y la compleja fórmula del equilibrio
articles.standfirst: Luis de la Fuente, ante el reto de ganar gestionando la carga de minutos de la mejor manera posible.
articles.summary: Luis de la Fuente, ante el reto de ganar gestionando la carga de minutos de la mejor manera posible.
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente se enfrenta a dos grandes retos durante esta ventana de selecciones. El primero es seguir ganando para alimentar la racha de imbatibilidad; el segundo es gestionar la carga de los futbolistas para seguir ganando sin que ninguno se resienta. Un equilibrio difícil de encontrar y que Luis de la Fuente está intentando gestionar de la mejor manera. La lista se complicó desde el principio. Y no precisamente por la mala gestión del seleccionador. Pedro Porro fue el primero en caerse de la lista inicial de 26. No llegó ni a viajar a Las Rozas porque se lesionó con el Tottenham y en su lugar llegó Iván Fresneda. Durante el calentamiento frente a Inglaterra cayó Eric García, que volvió a Barcelona para recuperarse allí; en el calentamiento del Pizjuán Grimaldo tuvo que parar y, tras ese partido en Sevilla, fueron Nico y Ferran los que sintieron molestias. Todos dejaron la concentración siguiendo la máxima del míster: "Riesgo cero". Una situación que le abrió las puertas del equipo a Robin Le Normand, Fran García y Carlos Espí. El nuevo escenario que se abría ante el seleccionador le obligaba a ser extremadamente cauteloso con la gestión de los minutos, así que ha optado por una equidad que a veces resulta compleja de ejecutar. Las rotaciones en el once son constantes. No ha repetido alineación en ninguno de los tres partidos de esta ventana y hemos visto caerse de la lista a indiscutibles como Cubarsí. Sin ir más lejos, en Oviedo rotó hasta el portero y Raya gozó de una oportunidad en detrimento de Unai Simón. El quiz de la cuestión reside en si es posible rotar tanto y competir con la misma fiabilidad: "Es difícil mantener el equilibrio entre los resultados y la salud de los jugadores. Hacemos lo que podemos. Los partidos hay que ganarlos, pero lo principal es la salud. A ver si no hay más lesiones. Seguro que de aquí al martes alguno va a notar más el cansancio. Los rivales también", reconoció el técnico tras la victoria contra la República Checa. Hasta el momento, el jugador más utilizado por De la Fuente ha sido Lamine Yamal. El extremo ha participado en los tres partidos jugando 203 minutos y con un registro de cuatro goles y dos asistencias. Fue titular en los tres encuentros completando los 90 minutos ante Inglaterra, una hora frente a Croacia y sólo 45 minutos ante la República Checa. Tras él aparece Rodri, con 185 minutos, y un grupo de cinco jugadores que han jugado dos partidos completos (180 minutos): Pubill, Cubarsí, Cucurella, Laporte y Unai Simón. A partir de ahí, Baena y Dani Olmo llevan 149, Fabián 127, Oyarzabal 126 o Pedri 120. También han debutado Fresneda y Roberto y hemos vivido un escenario poco habitual con sólo un mundialista (Laporte) formando parte del equipo que acabó el partido ante la República Checa. En la previa del partido ante Croacia, De la Fuente reveló la fórmula de los 270 minutos que ha intentado seguir en esta ventana de selecciones para no sobrecargar a los jugadores. "Siempre hemos sacado el mejor equipo para el partido que teníamos que enfrentar. Es lo que hemos hecho durante todo este torneo. Nadie va a jugar más de 270 minutos, que serían tres partidos de los cuatro. Es lo que jugarán la mayoría", explicó. Lo excepcional de todo esto reside en ser capaz de rotar de forma masiva y seguir ganando. Lo explicaba muy bien Mikel Merino: "Esta racha es histórica. Parece que los partidos se ganan como se comen pipas y no es para nada así. Cada partido es una batalla y es muy complicado llevarse la victoria. Hay que valorar lo que tenemos y seguir trabajando para que siga creciendo la racha". En Split, De la Fuente volverá a hacer cambios, pero veremos un once bastante parecido al de la final del Mundial en Nueva York. La oportunidad lo merece. Si España gana estará clasificada y se jugará la primera plaza del grupo con Inglaterra.

articles.title: Northern Ireland 0-0 Georgia: Liverpool's Giorgi Mamardashvili saves late Isaac Price penalty in Nations League stalemate
articles.summary: Match report from the UEFA Nations League Group B2 match between Northern Ireland and Georgia at Windsor Park; Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili saves Isaac Price's late penalty in stalemate
articles.body:
Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili guessed right to keep out Price's 84th-minute spot-kick after a combination of Nodar Lominadze and Saba Sazonov fouled Ruairi McConville as he sent a header against the crossbar during a goalmouth scramble.

Jamie Donley and Josh Magennis also brought saves out of Mamardashvili and Tom Atcheson felt he had should have had a first-half penalty, but Northern Ireland were held to a stalemate for the second time in a week at Windsor Park.

Georgia, still yet to score in this season's Nations League, responded to their 1-0 loss to Northern Ireland in Tbilisi 11 days ago by sacking Willy Sagnol, but Ramaz Svanadze is still awaiting his first win in charge despite Khvicha Kvaratskhelia showing flashes of his brilliance in the second half.

Northern Ireland started the night as the only side yet to concede in this season's Nations League, and Pierce Charles made big saves from Zuriko Davitashvili and Giorgi Tsitaishvili to make it four competitive clean sheets in a row for the first time since 2017.

The 21-year-old goalkeeper's seventh clean sheet in nine competitive appearances ensured Michael O'Neill's side remain top of Group B2 by a single point from Hungary.

Northern Ireland's confidence showed in their positive early intent but it took time to wear down a Georgia side who stubbornly defended their box.

McConville was first to test Mamardashvili as he met Justin Devenny's cross but his header was pushed to safety.

With the Northern Ireland fans singing 'Who are you?' at Ballon d'Or nominee Kvaratskhelia the visitors fashioned the clearest chance yet as Davitashvili wriggled free and hit a powerful strike that brought an excellent save from Pierce Charles.

Northern Ireland were soon back in the ascendancy, and when Trai Hume's long throw was allowed to bounce in the box, an improvised looping effort from Donley had Mamardashvili scrambling back.

Patrick Kelly then charged into the box but made the wrong choice in trying to find Donley as his cross was picked off, and Atcheson could not believe he was the one penalised in a clash with Sazonov but the decision was confirmed by a VAR check.

Northern Ireland struggled to replicate that fluidity after the break with some loose passing, and there was a further blow just after the hour when Ethan Galbraith, full of ideas on his return to the side after welcoming a baby boy, hobbled off.

Georgia were growing in confidence, and Pierce Charles did well to gather a deflected strike from Tsitaishvili before Kvaratskhelia blazed over.

It ended chaotically. When Shea Charles won the ball on the edge of the box it ran for Magennis who forced the save from Mamardashvili.

From the resulting corner, McConville got up but took a boot in the face Lominadze and a shove from Sazonov, with Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer awarding the penalty after being sent to the screen.

Price, who scored his first goal in 10 internationals against Ukraine on Friday, stepped up but it was a comfortable save for the Georgia goalkeeper.

With almost the last kick of the game, Georgia appealed in vain for a penalty after Callum Marshall collided with Sazonov in the corner of the Northern Ireland box.

articles.title: Defender jokes about facing Messi in international farewell 🎥
articles.summary: Benin national team defender Mohamed Tijani joked about the opportunity to face Lionel Messi in his farewell match for Argentina.Interviewed this Monday (5)...
articles.body:
Benin national team defender Mohamed Tijani joked about the opportunity to face Lionel Messi in his farewell match for Argentina.

Interviewed this Monday (5) while strolling through Buenos Aires, he admitted that he probably won't take the clash at the Monumental de Núñez too seriously.

"We don't have to mark him. We're going to enjoy the match. There's no special plan," he said.

During the conversation, the Benin player heaped praise on the Argentine star and said he is the best in the world.

Messi's farewell to the Argentine national team is scheduled for this Tuesday, in a friendly against the African side.

This final chapter will be written just over 21 years after the star made his debut for his country.

Messi's first match for Argentina took place in August 2005, against Hungary.

Since then, he has won two Copa América titles, as well as the World Cup.
